## STEP 33 — Mechanistic vs ML vs hybrid

**STEP ID:** 33

**TITLE:** Mechanistic vs ML vs hybrid. The single confirmatory three-arm comparison of Phase G, under condition shift, for a focused system.

**STATUS:** NOT STARTED. Gated on Step 32 G15-4 PASS (and Step 27 PASS if the mechanistic arm is the Step-26 simulator). No hybrid code exists. No D-C data.

**GOAL:** Test RQ15-3 (SSOT L18215) and G15-HYB / G15-5. Does a sequential hybrid (frozen mechanistic model + learned residual) add held-out-temperature, study-disjoint or calibration value beyond **both** the mechanistic model and the best pure-ML model? Or does it give a separately demonstrated physical-consistency advantage? Optionally, test whether a Step-28 E7 synthetic prior helps under the full G15-10 control set.

**SSOT ANCHORS:**
- §211.45–211.46 sequential hybrid (L19745–19770);
- §213.16–19 endpoint residual first, rate residual needs trajectories (L20864–20882); mandatory three-way benchmark and ‖f_NN‖ vs ‖f_known‖ (L20894–20912); "do not force residual small" (L20916–20924);
- §213.36 focused comparison set, headline split condition-OOD (L21106–21124); §213.43A multiplicative positive correction + residual-off ablation (L21195–21213);
- §215.30 "one of the highest-value advanced experiments" (L22325); §215.57 K6;
- §226.6 M4 (L24549–24558); §229.5 focused hypothesis (L25021–25033);
- G15-HYB (L22412–22414), G15-5 (L22386), G15-8 (L22389), G15-10 (L22391); §223.10–223.14 ratio sweep, TSTR, frozen rule (L24192–24255).

**SCIENTIFIC RATIONALE:**
- Hybrids should help where the mechanistic structure is right but incomplete (matrix effects, heat-transfer lag) and the data are time-resolved (von Stosch et al. 2014).
- The claim of extrapolation advantage over pure ML is testable only on held-out temperatures/times within a focused system.
- The SSOT makes it a three-arm, both-must-be-beaten test. That guards against "hybrid wins because the mechanistic arm was weak" and "hybrid wins because the residual swamps the mechanism".

**WHY NOW:** Only after Step 32 establishes an identifiable D8 (and Step 27 validates any simulator arm). Before that, the mechanistic arm is not credible and the comparison is meaningless (SSOT L24977 "Only after D8 is credible").

**INPUT ARTIFACTS:**
- Step 32 PARAM posteriors and K4 model (or the Step-27-validated SIM-AA-1 version);
- Step 30/31 best non-kinetic ML (same rows);
- Step 15 partitions (condition-OOD bands, study-disjoint);
- Step 28 E7 rows (only if Step 27 PASS) with full provenance;
- `phase_g_preregistration_v1.csv`.

**REQUIRED RESEARCH:** (a) Hybrid design practice. DONE (SSOT §213/§211 plus r_transition_ml Q7). (b) E7 controls. DONE (r_simulator_vv Q6: randomized-simulator control, real-n learning curve, calibration-leakage audit, provenance, Step-27-passed versions only). Nothing further.

**RESEARCH FINDINGS:**
- Simulator pretraining helped lake-temperature models only when the pretraining data spanned more variability than the real training period (Read et al. 2019, WRR; r_simulator_vv).
- Model-collapse risk is mainly for statistical/LLM generators (Shumailov et al. 2024).
- Kennedy–O'Hagan discrepancy is a principled residual form (Kennedy & O'Hagan 2001).

**ARCHITECTURE:**
- Three arms on identical rows/splits:
  - **(M)** mechanistic: Step-32 K4, or SIM-AA-1 in-domain;
  - **(ML)** best non-kinetic tabular from Steps 30/31: D5-tuned/D3-full with A4/A5 features;
  - **(H)** sequential hybrid: frozen M → residual r̂ trained on grouped folds (GBDT or D3-full on residuals); multiplicative positive form r = r_mech·exp(g(x)) for retention (SSOT L21203–21207); endpoint residual first; rate residual only with dense trajectories.
- Optional **(H-E7)** arm: ML or H pretrained on E7, real-finetuned, with:
  - ratio sweep 0/0.25/0.5/1/2/5×;
  - matched-volume randomized/wrong-physics simulator control;
  - real-n learning curve;
  - calibration-leakage audit;
  - TRTR/TSTR/mixed.
- Diagnostics:
  - ‖f_NN‖/‖f_mech‖ ratio;
  - residual-off ablation;
  - constraint violations (non-negativity, monotone degradation);
  - **semigroup test** T(t1+t2) ≈ T(t2)∘T(t1) under constant conditions (SSOT §212.52A L20537–20549; G15-8). M satisfies it by construction; ML and H may not.
- Reaction-network (G15-RXN) arms are **out of scope** here. Any CRNN/SINDy work is a simulator-recovery study under Step 28 (SSOT L21211).

**DO:**
- One pre-registered confirmatory comparison: primary metric = held-out-temperature ln-retention MAE; primary split = condition-OOD ∩ study-disjoint.
- Holm across the two pairwise tests (H vs M, H vs ML).
- Report extrapolation error vs horizon.

**DO NOT:**
- Fit jointly first (rejected as the first hybrid; SSOT §211.45).
- Tune on test.
- Let E7 rows into calibration/test (frozen rule).
- Report the best ratio only.
- Rename learned interactions as mechanisms.

**OUTPUT ARTIFACTS:**
- `experiments/EXP-0000NN/`;
- `reports/step33/three_arm_results.md`;
- `reports/step33/g15_hyb_record.md`;
- `reports/step33/g15_10_ratio_sweep.md` (if E7 used);
- `reports/step33/semigroup_consistency.md`;
- §216.13 items 5 and 7.

**DATA REQUIREMENTS:** Step 32 data, plus ≥2 held-out temperature bands across ≥K_33 independent groups (PROPOSED K_33 = 5, cf. r_eval_splits "<5 validation studies → RESEARCH_ONLY").

**BASELINES:** M and ML arms are the baselines. Persistence and D4 are reported for context.

**EXPERIMENTS / ABLATIONS:** E33-1 three-arm; E33-2 residual-off; E33-3 additive vs multiplicative residual; E33-4 E7 ratio sweep + randomized-simulator control + learning curve; E33-5 semigroup/constraint diagnostics.

**METRICS:**
- MAE (ln-retention); trajectory RMSE;
- interval coverage/width; CRPS;
- constraint-violation rate; semigroup violation magnitude;
- extrapolation error vs ΔT from the training range;
- ‖f_NN‖/‖f_mech‖.

**LEAKAGE CONTROLS:**
- Residual model trained only on training groups.
- Simulator calibration studies ⊂ downstream training studies.
- E7 generated only from the Step-27-passed sim_version, with provenance fields `sim_model_id, sim_version, validation_status, param_draw_seed, domain_flag`.
- Held-out bands untouched by any arm's tuning.

**UNCERTAINTY / CONFIDENCE:** MEDIUM on design. LOW on reaching the step within the plan horizon (data-gated twice).

**COMPUTE:** CPU sufficient; GPU unnecessary even for small residual MLPs at this n; A100 unnecessary.

**HUMAN REVIEW:** Expert interprets residual structure (≈6 h). Kush signs the G15-HYB record.

**LICENCE / ACCESS:** As Step 32. E7 rows are internal derived data, never released as evidence.

**PASS GATE** (pre-registered):
- **G33 (G15-HYB):** H beats **both** M and ML on the primary split with Holm-adjusted paired-cluster LB > δ_33 (PROPOSED_PILOT), without coverage below c_floor; **or** H shows a pre-declared physical-consistency advantage (constraint/semigroup violations reduced by ≥ a pre-registered margin) at non-inferior error.
- **G15-5:** M or H beats ML on held-out temperature (same rule).
- **G15-10** (if E7 used): real-only study-disjoint improvement survives the full ratio sweep, beats the randomized-simulator control, and keeps calibration within c_floor.
- The step passes once the comparison is decided. A loss for H is a valid result.

**FAIL ACTION:**
- H fails → keep the simpler winner (M or ML) in the registry and the C9/MODEL rung (law; SSOT §215.69).
- M fails vs ML on held-out T (G15-5 no) → kinetic structure is RESEARCH_ONLY for prediction (it is still usable for mechanistic explanation in packets as MECHANISTIC BACKGROUND).
- E7 fails G15-10 → E7 stays restricted to identifiability and stress tests; no pretraining claim.

**FALLBACK:** If <K_33 groups: run as a descriptive within-study extrapolation study. No G15-HYB claim.

**PARALLEL WORK:** Step 34a (independent data); Step 35; Step 36.

**NEXT IF PASS:** Step 34b (in-domain rollout using the winning arm). Step 36 MODEL rung for the system (IN_VALIDATION_DOMAIN only).

**STOP FOR REVIEW:** After the pre-registration (before the first held-out read) and after the G15-HYB record.

## STEP 34 — Short rollout

**STEP ID:** 34 (substeps 34a, 34b, 34c)

**TITLE:** Short rollout:
- composition/semigroup consistency on existing multi-step endpoints (34a);
- true trust-horizon evaluation where real intermediate states exist (34b);
- rollout abstention interface (34c).

**STATUS:**
- NOT STARTED.
- **34a is feasible now:** USDA has 1,429 rows with ≥2 process steps and PE 195, composite start→end with no intermediate state (r_transition_ml diagnostic).
- **34b is NEED_DATA:** EVD has no true intermediate state (r_transition_ml). There are no D-C staged sequences. Step-19 Gold trajectories do not exist (existing Gold is AI-assisted and not independent).

**GOAL:**
- 34a: Test whether chaining one-step transition predictions reproduces observed composite endpoints (G15-8 composition consistency). This is a cheap falsification test of one-step models used in sequences.
- 34b: Establish an empirical trust horizon H_trust (SSOT L20556–20566) for the winning one-step model on real held-out sequences with measured intermediates:
  - quantitative R2 only for a focused system with staged measurements;
  - qualitative/procedural R0/R1 on Step-19 Gold trajectories.
- 34c: Define the rollout abstention rule that Step 36 consumes.

**SSOT ANCHORS:**
- Permanent rule 3 "one-step prediction does not establish rollout stability" (L18015–18031);
- §212 exposure bias and multi-step loss (L19907–19949); scheduled sampling / denoising ablations (L20073–20091); rollout abstention triggers (L20149–20158); "must not silently continue" (L20125);
- horizon coverage (L20192–20208); trajectory error (L20210–20222); constraint violations (L20224–20234);
- R0–R5 fidelity ladder (L20400–20424); M0–M11 (L20481–20507); strong sparse symbolic baseline (L20509–20523); retrieval-augmented transition loop (L20525–20535);
- semigroup test (L20537–20549); H_trust (L20556–20566); provenance graph (L20567–20581);
- staged experiment value (L20426–20439);
- §215.16–17 E(k), D(k) (L22142–22165); §215.31 (L22329); §216.4 rollout table (L22847–22863);
- G15-8 (L22389), G15-11 (L22392).

**SCIENTIFIC RATIONALE:**
- Errors compound and inputs drift under free rollout (Venkatraman, Hebert & Bagnell 2015, AAAI). The system's own dynamics shape compounding (Lambert et al., preprint).
- A trust horizon is meaningful only against real intermediate states (G15-11).
- 34a is a legitimate, data-available proxy that can *refute* sequential use of one-step models. It cannot establish a horizon.

**WHY NOW:**
- 34a can run immediately after Step 30. It needs only the one-step winner and the multi-step rows.
- 34b waits for Step 33 (focused system) and/or Step 19 (Gold trajectories).
- 34c must exist before Step 36's MODEL rung handles multi-step queries.

**INPUT ARTIFACTS:**
- Step 30/31 one-step winners;
- EVD multi-step rows with `process.steps` / `step_process_ids`;
- the USDA R6 documentation (multiplicativity check);
- for 34b: staged-sequence evidence in KIN/SEQ (`ledgers/data/SEQ.jsonl`, new, §216.4 schema) from Steps 11–14, the Step-33 winner, and Step-19 Gold trajectories (`state_observed`, `observation_quality`);
- Step 18 event-sourcing engine for R0/R1.

**REQUIRED RESEARCH:**
- (a) Are USDA multi-step retention factors themselves computed by multiplying single-step factors (circularity)? OPEN. Answer by reading the R6 documentation inside Step 34a.0 (a cheap, decisive check), not by external search.
- (b) Do staged-cooking datasets with intermediate measurements exist? OPEN (ssot_l15a Q5). Asked as a Step-13 discovery query.

**RESEARCH FINDINGS:**
- DaD-style multi-step training bounds compounding error (Venkatraman et al. 2015). Scheduled sampling is an ablation (SSOT L20073).
- One-step conformal ≠ trajectory coverage (SSOT L20194).
- Reaction-network or neural rollout (M10/M11) needs dense trajectories: deferred.
- The symbolic deterministic baseline plus the retrieval-augmented loop is "likely highly competitive" (SSOT L20509–20535).

**ARCHITECTURE:**
- **34a.0** Circularity check on USDA multi-step factors. If they are multiplicative derivations, USDA is excluded from 34a (PE only) and the exclusion is recorded.
- **34a.1** For composite rows (start → P1 → P2 → end), compare:
  - M0 persistence;
  - M1 composite-lookup (D4 on the composite process signature);
  - M2-chain: one-step winner applied P1 then P2 with state carried through (multiplicative composition for retention).
- Metrics: composite error; D(2) proxy = E(chain)/E(one-step on single-step rows); propagated-interval coverage by Monte Carlo through one-step conformal/posterior draws; constraint violations; semigroup violation where conditions are constant.
- **34b** (data-gated):
  - M0–M2 first, then M7 (uncertainty-aware) and M9 (event + local kinetics, using the Step-33 winner);
  - the symbolic procedure-state updater + retrieval loop as the strong baseline;
  - E(1..K), D(k), horizon-wise coverage, E_traj;
  - H_trust with c_min, ε_max, τ pre-registered and **calibrated on held-out calibration sequences distinct from test sequences**;
  - K = 2–3 steps.
  - R0/R1 on Step-19 Gold: qualitative state accuracy vs horizon, using the Step-18 engine. Owner of the procedural engine is 18/19; Step 34 only evaluates the horizon.
- **34c** Rollout abstention spec: stop or downgrade to a QUALITATIVE claim when any of these hold: evidence distance > τ; interval width > ε_max; constraint violation; horizon k > H_trust; or the input state is inferred rather than observed (SSOT L20149–20158). This plugs into the Step-36 cascade DIRECT → INTERPOLATE → MODEL → QUALITATIVE → ASK → ABSTAIN.
- **G15-11 scope rule (SCR-G-1):** a D-D (recipe Gold) pass licenses R0/R1 only, never R2+ (SSOT L21994–21996).

**DO:**
- Report D(k), not just final error.
- Keep procedural rollout metrics separate from chemistry metrics (SSOT L22177).
- Log provenance per predicted transition (§212.53 fields).

**DO NOT:**
- Claim a trust horizon from 34a.
- Treat recipe text as quantitative intermediates.
- Train long-horizon neural rollouts.
- Use one-step coverage as trajectory coverage.
- Let a rollout continue past H_trust.

**OUTPUT ARTIFACTS:**
- `reports/step34/usda_multistep_circularity_check.md`;
- `reports/step34/composition_consistency_34a.md`;
- `reports/step34/trust_horizon_34b.md` (when data exist);
- `ledgers/data/SEQ.jsonl` schema adoption (§216.4) coordinated with Step 18;
- `reports/step34/rollout_abstention_spec_v1.md` (34c, consumed by Step 36);
- §216.13 item 8.

**DATA REQUIREMENTS:**
- 34a: existing EVD multi-step rows.
- 34b: ≥K_34 (PROPOSED 5) independent studies with measured state after each of ≥2 stages (e.g. blanch→freeze→cook) for one system, or a project staged experiment (none planned; no lab, UNVERIFIED). Step-19 Deep Gold trajectories for R0/R1.

**BASELINES:** M0 persistence; M1 composite lookup; symbolic deterministic updater + retrieval (34b).

**EXPERIMENTS / ABLATIONS:**
- E34a-1: chain vs composite-lookup vs persistence;
- E34a-2: semigroup violations;
- E34b-1: teacher-forced vs free rollout;
- E34b-2: scheduled sampling / noisy-state ablation, only if a learned multi-step model is used;
- E34b-3: retrieval-corrected vs open-loop (SSOT L20057–20071).

**METRICS:** Composite MAE; D(k); horizon-wise coverage/width; E_traj; constraint-violation counts by category (SSOT L20224–20234); H_trust with cluster CI; abstention precision/recall on unsupported horizons.

**LEAKAGE CONTROLS:**
- Composite rows and their single-step constituents from the same lineage component stay in one fold. Otherwise the chain trivially reproduces the composite.
- Calibration sequences are disjoint from test sequences.
- Gold trajectories are never seen by models they score (blind Deep Gold).

**UNCERTAINTY / CONFIDENCE:** 34a MEDIUM (the circularity check may void USDA). 34b LOW (data). 34c HIGH (spec).

**COMPUTE:** CPU sufficient; A100 unnecessary.

**HUMAN REVIEW:** Expert reads the R6 documentation for the multiplicativity question (≈1–2 h). Kush signs the abstention spec. Step-19 annotation hours are owned by Step 19.

**LICENCE / ACCESS:** As Steps 29/32. Recipe Gold is subject to the recipe-source licences (A1 local-only; Food.com uploader-declared CC0).

**PASS GATE:**
- **G34a (G15-8 composition):** the report exists with a pre-registered verdict. "Chain-consistent" iff the chain's composite error is ≤ (1+ρ)× the composite-lookup error with ρ PROPOSED_PILOT, and propagated 90% coverage ≥ c_floor. Either verdict passes; a failure is a retained negative ("one-step models must not be chained").
- **G34b (G15-11):** H_trust established with cluster CI on real held-out sequences: quantitative R2 for the focused system; R0/R1 only for D-D. Otherwise "no rollout claim".
- **G34c:** abstention spec frozen and consumed by the Step-36 tests.

**FAIL ACTION:**
- 34a inconsistent → Step 36 must not chain one-step model outputs. Multi-step queries go to composite-evidence lookup or QUALITATIVE.
- 34b no data → NEED_DATA. Request staged-sequence studies via the Step-13 discovery query and the Step-14 quotas. The Step-36 rollout rung stays disabled.
- H_trust = 1 → only single-step MODEL answers are allowed.

**FALLBACK:** Procedural-only rollout (R0) via the Step-18 engine with no quantitative state, labelled as such.

**PARALLEL WORK:** 34a parallel with Steps 31–33; 34c parallel with Step 36 design.

**NEXT IF PASS:** Step 36 (cascade with H_trust and abstention spec). Any inverse design (sub-step of 36; G15-12/G15-INV) needs these forward-credibility records.

**STOP FOR REVIEW:** After 34a.0 (circularity verdict) and after the abstention spec.

### GOAL
Produce, for each level (molecule, ingredient, ingredient-state, recipe, cuisine), the **simplest representation that
survives leakage-safe, non-circular, confound-controlled evaluation**, registered as **typed similarity notions that are
never fused into one scalar**, plus two decision records (Level-12 §183.4, Level-13 §193.8) stating what each
representation means, which tasks it supports, and what it does **not** support (SSOT L13275, L15276). These records
are the only legitimate input of representations to Step 36 (CulinaryState-RAG and FlavorTwin).

### SCIENTIFIC RATIONALE
1. Small-data molecular property prediction: fingerprints + trees are rarely beaten by learned/pretrained encoders
   (MoleculeNet, Wu et al. Chem Sci 2018; Deng et al. Nat Commun 14:6395, 2023; Praski et al. arXiv 2508.06199 —
   **preprint**, though SSOT F3 L10671 labels it FROZEN). MOL has 1.7k molecules → firmly small-data.
2. Structure ≠ perception: single-molecule odour maps generalise (Lee et al. Science 2023, POM), but mixtures are
   poorly predicted from components (Snitz et al. PLoS CB 2013; Ravia et al. Nature 2020) and no public
   ingredient-level sensory labels exist (r_representation_flavortwin Q2). Therefore ingredient sensory similarity is
   UNSUPPORTED, not "low confidence".
3. Food-pairing statistics are cultural descriptors dominated by ingredient frequency (Jain, Rakhi & Bagler, PLoS One
   10:e0139539, 2015; Spence, Food Res Int 2020); frequency-preserving nulls are mandatory before any claim.
4. Presence ≠ abundance ≠ importance (SSOT L11459): repo IMAP is 98% presence-only, 0 thresholds → Regime A only; OAV
   (Regime C) impossible today.
5. Recipe/cuisine: learned set/sequence encoders must beat incidence/IDF/mean-pooling under frequency/size/source
   controls (§194.3). Near-duplicate leakage inflates recipe metrics (Lee et al. ACL 2022; Allamanis 2019) →
   recall-oriented split groups and a kNN memorisation baseline are required.
6. Cuisine supervision is weak: 9.81% explicit labels, Food.com 0%, and 153/156 labelled REC sources carry a single
   cuisine label → cuisine ≈ source/book (ssot_l13 §5.2). Cuisine classification headlines would be source
   classification (SSOT §194.2 risk 2, L15298).

start as a **parallel lane** once those exist, not after Phase G. Rationale: SSOT L169 (L12 "CORE EXECUTION
PRIORITY"), L13219–13244 (Phase 0 early), L27732 (L12 "PARALLEL"), MP L237 (B04 parallel after B02), and §216.10
(L15 does not need L12, so 29–34 do not wait on 35 and 35 explicit rungs need not wait on 29–34). The learned rungs
(35g) and the process-conditioned notion (35f) stay late, because they need non-circular supervised targets and
validated transition outputs (Steps 27/30/33) that do not exist.

### RESEARCH FINDINGS
(Sources and confidence from research notes; I re-verified SSOT §246 text and repo counts this run.)
- [HIGH] ECFP4/Morgan + RF/LightGBM/logistic + kNN-Tanimoto is the right default z_m^struct; pretrained encoders are
  optional rungs (MoleculeNet 2018; Deng 2023; Praski 2025/26 preprint). → SSOT change request on F3 evidence label.
- [HIGH] Molecule-level sensory prediction is defensible (POM 2023; DREAM, Keller et al. Science 2017;
  fingerprint+XGBoost competitive, Suh et al. Commun Chem 8:278, 2025). Mixture/ingredient sensory prediction is not
  supported by public data (POMMix is an AI4MAT-ICLR-2025 **workshop** preprint; AROMMA 2026 preprint; Ravia 2020 lab
  mixtures only).
- [HIGH] Pairing ≠ palatability; frequency is the dominant confound (Ahn et al. Sci Rep 2011; Jain, Rakhi & Bagler
  PLoS One 2015 — note: not Sci Rep; Spence 2020). Curveball (Strona et al. Nat Commun 5:4114, 2014) gives exact
  degree-preserving nulls at >10^8 cells (CPU).
- [MEDIUM] Aggregators: Deep Sets / Set Transformer / OTKE need supervised targets; no food-specific OT evidence found
  (SSOT "Unverified" at L8868 stands). SSOT's own example shows aggregator choice matters more than the kernel
  (L8306–8330) → aggregator ablation with cardinality slope is the first experiment, not a learned encoder.
- [HIGH] Data: FlavorDB (Garg et al. NAR 2018) = 25,595 molecules / 936 ingredients presence-only — SSOT §175.3
  (L10690) attributes these to FlavorDB2 (error). Repo IMAP: 31,334 presence edges, 219 measured concentrations
  (polyphenols, not odorants), 0 thresholds → OAV NEED_DATA.
- [MEDIUM] Recipe/cuisine: no new primary evidence changes R0–R9/C0–C8; KitcheNette (IJCAI 2019) and RecipeMind
  (CIKM 2022) train and evaluate on co-occurrence-derived targets → circular as headlines (§133.2); "Kissing
  Cuisines" WWW'17 record carries a 2026 Crossref removal notice → do not cite.
- [HIGH] Identity/leakage: published dedup thresholds are tool defaults or proxy-label optima (Lee 2022; Allamanis
  2019; RecipeNLG, Bień et al. INLG 2020) → must be human-calibrated (07I-C); split groups must be recall-oriented,
  identity relations precision-oriented (Broder 1997: resemblance not transitive). Add kNN memorisation baseline
  (Allamanis 2019).
- [HIGH] L13E is parallel; copy-mutate parameters are not identifiable from rank-frequency (Kinouchi et al. 2008 own
  statement; Tuwani et al. 2019 null reproduces category curves) → SBI/pretraining deferred; G13E-01 fails for
  temporal claims (Food.com year = upload year; Gutenberg era = author-birth proxy).
- [MEDIUM] FlavorTwin related work 2024–2026 (FlavorGraph Sci Rep 2021; FlavorDiffusion 2025 workshop; Epicure
  preprints 2026; GISMo 2023; FoodPuzzle KDD 2025; FlavourBench 2026 preprint; Tac et al. 2026 preprint; Tagkopoulos et
  al. 2026 preprint; NotCo US10957424B1) narrows novelty to evidence-gated state/process-aware inverse search with
  typed similarities and non-circular evaluation (see parts file §O).
- [HIGH] Statistics: paired cluster bootstrap over the unit of independence; cluster sign-flip permutation when
  <~20–30 clusters (Cameron et al. 2008); no fold-SE CIs (Bates et al. 2023); nested grouped tuning (Cawley & Talbot
  2010); Holm (confirmatory)/BH (exploratory); sealed test with access log (r_eval_splits).

### ARCHITECTURE
"Typed Similarity Registry + gated representation ladder", CPU-first:
```
35.0 pre-registration + contract intake ─┬─ 35a molecule features & leaderboard (E2/E3, ref = ECFP4-count+LightGBM)
                                          ├─ 35b ingredient chemical profile x_ij (tiered) + aggregator ablation (E0–E3)
                                          ├─ 35c recipe R0, R1*, R2-explicit, R3 (where CQPO exists) + frequency panel
                                          ├─ 35d cuisine C0–C2 + motifs + matched resampling (+ cuisine ontology draft)
                                          └─ 35-E (optional) L13E descriptive/null lane (E13E-01, -04, -02; -03 if licensed)
                 35e typed similarity registry v2 (9 notions) + separation tests (SX-14-02) + nulls
                 35f process-conditioned notion (consumes Steps 15/27/30/33; analytes with evidence only)
                 35g learned rungs E4–E8 / R4–R9 / C3–C8 / O1–O7 — GATED, default DEFER
                 35h Level-12 + Level-13 decision records + FlavorTwin/RAG hand-off manifest
```
(*R1 uses an explicit, non-learned z_i — the 35b profile — and is labelled as such; a text-embedding z_i is an
ablation only, per L14906.)
Rules: (i) every similarity is a registered function `sim_id → (notion, level, formula, aggregator, null_model,
eval_set, split_family, valid_domain, evidence_class_required, licence_scope, status)`; (ii) fusion only as a
task-conditioned reranker that reports per-notion components, never stored as "the similarity" (§246.2); (iii) UNKNOWN
concentration/role/state is masked, never 0 (§192.9 L15082); (iv) L12 T8/T9 process-chemistry threads are **homed in
Steps 29–34** (they duplicate them); 35f only consumes their promoted, validated outputs.

### BASELINES
- Molecule: label-frequency prior; kNN-Tanimoto (k pre-registered); **ECFP4 count + LightGBM** (reference, G2);
  ECFP bit + RF; logistic/ridge on ECFP; PubChem-881 + LightGBM (data already present); descriptors (RDKit2D) +
  LightGBM; TabPFN optional CPU comparator (licence recorded; v2 weights terms as per Hollmann et al. Nature 2025);
  OpenPOM MPNN reproduction = mandatory SOTA comparator **only if** odour tasks are licensed (L11036).
- Ingredient: E0 n_ij; E1 Jaccard / Ochiai / IDF overlap + null percentile; E2 kernel-mean Tanimoto, symmetrised
  best-match, top-k mean; E3 descriptor-space aggregation; OT one ablation arm; bag-of-compounds + LightGBM.
- Recipe: R0 incidence Jaccard/cosine; R2-explicit TF-IDF; R1 mean of explicit z_i; R3 quantity-weighted (Food.com/A1
  subset only); **frequency-only shortcut**; **kNN memorisation baseline**; LightGBM/logistic over R0/R2.
- Cuisine: C0 prevalence; C1 specificity/TF-IDF; C2 pair/triplet motifs (support thresholds); §85 classical
  fingerprint; C3 mean recipe vector (explicit).
- Cultural/pairing: U, F, C, FC, E nulls + Curveball.
- Learned rungs (35g) compared against the strongest of the above on identical splits.

### METRICS
Molecule: macro AUROC, macro AUPRC (primary for rare labels), per-label F1, ECE/Brier, OOD gap (random − scaffold).
Ingredient/recipe retrieval & completion: Recall@K, MRR, nDCG@K, Hit@K, frequency-stratified macro Recall; masked
reconstruction AUPRC. Cuisine: macro-F1 (with minimum class support pre-registered), held-out prevalence JSD, motif
AUPRC. Similarity diagnostics: cardinality slope ρ(score, |profile|), null percentile/ΔN_s with CI and BH q, inter-notion
rank agreement, kNN-overlap@k, stability (bootstrap neighbour overlap, CKA/Procrustes for embeddings).
All: paired cluster-bootstrap CI of differences (cluster = scaffold cluster / ingredient cluster / split_group /
source), seeds ≥5 × folds ≥5 (G3 default), compute (params, wall time, RAM).

### LEAKAGE CONTROLS
- Molecules: InChIKey full + connectivity-layer disjointness; stereo-undefined molecules grouped with their
  stereoisomers; pretraining-corpus overlap recorded for any pretrained encoder (T4 risk L10829).
- Ingredients: ingredient-cluster-disjoint (raw/cooked/cultivar variants of one food in one fold — r_eval_splits).
- Recipes: `split_group_id` (07I-C) disjoint; cross-split groups = 0 (§257G.9 L34857); Gold firewall groups excluded
  from training; kNN memorisation baseline as leakage alarm; residual cross-split max IDF-Jaccard reported.
- Cuisine: source-disjoint where ≥3 labelled sources; cuisine features never use the held-out cuisine (A_i^c

### PASS GATE
(Thresholds marked † are PROPOSED_PILOT and must be pre-registered by humans in 35.0 before any run; no post-hoc change.)
- **G35-PRE**: pre-registration committed and hashed before the first evaluation run; access log for sealed tests.
- **G35-0** (= SSOT G0 + G13-0): split manifests frozen and hashed; zero InChIKey (full and connectivity) overlap across
  molecule splits; cross-split Tanimoto NN distribution reported; zero split_group crossings; kNN memorisation
  baseline reported for every recipe task.
- **G35-COV**: for every ingredient/recipe similarity arm the cardinality slope is reported with CI; if |ρ| > 0.3† and it
  persists under matched-coverage resampling, the arm is flagged COVERAGE_CONFOUNDED and cannot be a headline.
- **G35-CIRC**: zero headline results in a "circular/weak" row of L14700–14709 / L8476–8482 (audited table).
- **G35-SEP**: every one of the nine notions has a registry row with its own eval set, null model and split family, or is
  explicitly status UNSUPPORTED / NEED_DATA; separation test report published; no fused scalar exists in any output.
- **G35-NULL** (= G13E-06 applied to Step 35): every cultural/co-occurrence/pairing claim survives F and FC nulls and
  Curveball, BH q < 0.05†, effect CI excluding 0, and mapped-coverage audit; else claim narrowed/dropped.
- **Promotion rule** (SSOT §183.3, §194.3, G13-1, G3): a more complex rung is promoted only if the paired
  cluster-bootstrap lower 95% CI bound of its gain over the strongest simpler comparator exceeds δ† (molecule:
  0.01 macro-AUROC / 0.02 macro-AUPRC per SSOT G3 "proposed"; retrieval: 0.01 Recall@10†) on ≥2 task families and two
  split types, and survives frequency/size/source controls. With <20–30 clusters use cluster sign-flip permutation.
- **Completion**: `level12_decision_record_v1.md` covers all 12 §183.4 boxes and `level13_decision_record_v1.md` all 12
  §193.8 boxes, each marked PROMOTED / FAILED / DATA-BLOCKED (L13275 allows "data-blocked"). Step 35 PASSES when the
  explicit-rung records are complete and all G35-* gates pass — **learned rungs are not required for PASS**.

### FAIL ACTION
- G35-PRE fails → no run; fix pre-registration.
- G35-0 fails (leakage) → stop evaluation; repair splits (07I-C or molecule grouping); rerun all affected baselines; old
  numbers marked INVALID_LEAKAGE, retained in history.
- G35-COV flags → notion keeps BASELINE status with "coverage-confounded" label; route to Step 12/14 acquisition
  (more profiles / concentrations) rather than to a more complex aggregator.
- G35-CIRC fails → headline withdrawn; replace with a non-circular task from the matrix.
- G35-SEP fails for a notion → notion status UNSUPPORTED; Step 36 may not expose it.
- G35-NULL fails → pairing/cultural claim narrowed or dropped; FlavorTwin cultural prior not enabled.
- Learned rung fails promotion → explicit rung remains default (valid negative result, SSOT L13258, L14938).
- G7/G3 cannot be evaluated (no sensory labels) → sensory notions stay HYPOTHESIS/UNSUPPORTED; acquisition request to
  Step 06/12 (licensed GS-LF/Keller) or human decision to keep FlavorTwin sensory scope out.

### FALLBACK
If 07I-C is late: use the conservative permissive grouping (exact ∪ provisional family ∪ dish-family candidate, or
source-level) for splits so leakage control never waits on calibration (r_l13e_identity §4). If rdkit is not approved:
run 35a on PubChem-881 + descriptors only and record that SIM-06 remains DATA-MISSING. If licences block molecule
labels: 35a reduces to structural-similarity infrastructure + taste tasks only. Minimal viable Step 35 = 35.0, 35b,
35c, 35e, 35h (explicit rungs + registry + records).

### PARALLEL WORK
Explicit substeps (35.0–35e, 35-E) run in parallel with Steps 08–15 and 16–20 and 21–34 once Step 04 contracts and
07I-C groups exist. 35f waits for 27/30/33; 35g waits for 35a–35e results and a non-circular target. No step in 08–34
consumes Step 35 outputs (§216.10; SSOT L45449 for L13E).

### NEXT IF PASS
Step 36 consumes `similarity_registry_v2.csv`, the two decision records and `flavortwin_rag_handoff_v1.md`: RAG may use
only notions with status BASELINE/PROMOTED for the tasks the records list; FlavorTwin static baselines (§246.8) are
built from 35a–35e; process-conditioned FlavorTwin waits for 35f + Step 27/33 + volatile evidence (NEED_DATA).

### STOP FOR REVIEW
Stop and request human review at: (1) pre-registration sign-off (35.0); (2) licence decisions before any molecule-label
or Food.com-trained model; (3) after 35b/35c first results (to decide whether OT/learned aggregators stay in plan);
(4) before any 35g GPU run; (5) before the decision records are frozen; (6) before Step 36 consumes anything.

in Step 36 require registered, evaluated similarity notions; the L12/L13 completion gates require decision records.
Without Step 35, Step 36 would either use unvalidated embeddings (violates §216.10/§194.3) or none.

**SCIENTIFIC QUESTION** — Which representation of molecules, ingredients, recipes and cuisines adds measurable
information beyond explicit classical statistics on non-circular held-out tasks, and how far apart are the nine
similarity notions empirically?

**ENGINEERING QUESTION** — How to compute, version and serve nine typed similarity functions over 1.7k molecules,
~313 profiled ingredients (5,387 canonical), 612k recipes and ~256 raw cuisine labels with streamable CPU pipelines,
leakage-safe split manifests and per-notion provenance/licence scope.

**KNOWN EVIDENCE** — RESEARCH FINDINGS above; repo DATA REQUIREMENTS table.

**UNKNOWN / UNCERTAIN** — OT vs kernel-mean on real profile-size distributions; strength of coverage confounding in
FlavorGraph presence profiles (313 of 5,387 ING profiled); legal status of odour label sets; size distribution of
permissive split groups (giant-component risk); whether Food.com Keywords contain cuisine tags; Food.com near-duplicate
rate; whether any ingredient-level sensory dataset with licence fit exists (none found). Not forced to numbers.

**CONFIDENCE** — MEDIUM (step); HIGH (ladder/order/placement); LOW (sensory, process-conditioned flavour).

**RESEARCH REQUIRED? / COMPLETED / RESULT** — Required: yes (model family, data availability, novelty). Completed:
r_representation_flavortwin, r_l13e_identity, r_eval_splits + this run's pyrfume licence check. Result: architecture
choice settled (stop rule §8.1, §8.5); residual uncertainty is empirical → pilot P35-0 (CPU, ~1–2 agent-days, local data
only, after rdkit approval) is cheaper than more reading.

**ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED** — (a) single universal flavour embedding à la FlavorGraph/Epicure — rejected (§246.2; Epicure
shows entangled taste/geography/processing/culture); (b) pretrained molecular foundation model as default z_m —
rejected (small-data evidence); (c) Deep Sets/Set Transformer/OT as default aggregator — rejected until a supervised
non-circular target exists; (d) KitcheNette/RecipeMind-style co-occurrence-trained pairing — baseline only; (e) Recipe1M

top-level step — rejected (brief §4 A–D not met; substep parallelisation suffices); (h) OAV-weighted sensory similarity
now — rejected (would invent values).

**SIMPLE BASELINE / STRONG BASELINE / OPTIONAL ADVANCED MODEL**
- Simple: label prior, kNN-Tanimoto, n_ij/Jaccard/IDF, R0 incidence, C0 prevalence, frequency-only shortcut.
- Strong: ECFP4-count + LightGBM; kernel-mean / best-match aggregation; R2-explicit TF-IDF + LightGBM; C1/C2

### Brief §0 per-step questions
| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Objective correct? | Yes, if read as "earn representations against explicit baselines and keep notions typed"; wrong if read as "train embeddings". |
| Necessary? | Yes — FlavorTwin static baselines and L12/L13 completion records need it; Step 36 must not consume unvalidated embeddings. |
| Placed correctly? | Partly. Learned/process-conditioned rungs belong late; explicit rungs, splits and registry belong in a parallel lane from ~Step 07I-C/04 onward (SSOT L169, L27732, MP L237). |
| Dependencies correct? | The serial chain 34→35 is not an artifact dependency (§216.10). True hard deps: 04, 06, 07I-C; 15/27/30/33 only for 35f; 16–20 only for R3-role/procedural. |
| Data requirement realistic? | Explicit rungs: yes. Sensory/OAV/process-conditioned flavour: no (NEED_DATA). Cuisine: weak (9.81%, ≈source). |
| Architecture sound? | Yes with the typed registry, circularity audit and nulls; SSOT already specifies it well. |
| Baselines appropriate? | Yes; add kNN memorisation, frequency-only, Curveball null, LLM/GISMo baselines (FlavorTwin, Step 36). |
| Metrics sufficient? | Add cardinality slope, null percentile, inter-notion agreement, paired cluster-bootstrap differences. |
| Gates meaningful? | SSOT gates are mostly unthresholded; G3/G4/G7 need unavailable sensory labels → rewrite for available tasks + pre-register (G35-*). |
| Literature suggests better approach? | No better default; literature confirms simple-first. Novelty narrowed by 2024–2026 work. |
| Simpler approach sufficient? | Likely yes for v1: explicit rungs may be the final result (valid). |
| Missing artifact? | Similarity registry v2, representation registry, split_group_id, cuisine ontology, x_ij tiers, decision records. |
| Duplicating another step? | Yes: L12 T8/T9 duplicates 29–34 → re-home. E13E-05 duplicates 07I calibration → moved to 07I-C. |
| Parallel-safe? | Yes for explicit rungs (CPU, recipe/molecule planes, no writes to evidence plane). |
| Reducible? | Minimal viable = 35.0, 35b, 35c, 35e, 35h. |
| Research before implementation? | No more reading needed; run P35-0 pilot after approval. |
| STOP/MODIFY/KEEP/NEED_DATA triggers | STOP: leakage (G35-0) or circular headline. MODIFY: coverage-confounded arms → acquisition, not complexity. KEEP: explicit rung wins. NEED_DATA: sensory, OAV, volatile process-conditioned, temporal L13E. |

## A. STEP 36 — parent card

**STEP ID**
36. Substeps: 36.0, 36A, 36B, 36C and 36D. Numbering is preserved and no new top-level step is added.

**TITLE**
Evidence compiler → selective CulinaryState-RAG → later FlavorTwin

**STATUS**

**GOAL**
Turn the shared state, evidence, transition and uncertainty core into an application that does three things:
1. **Compile query-specific, provenance-bearing evidence packets** (the evidence compiler).
2. **Answer selectively.** It answers, compares, asks, diagnoses, recovers, recommends or abstains through an explicit support cascade, DIRECT → INTERPOLATE → MODEL → QUALITATIVE → ASK → ABSTAIN. Conflict is reported as an orthogonal status. Output precision never exceeds evidence precision (SSOT L26425–26431), and every claim is traceable (G16-PROV).
3. **Later, reuse the same core for FlavorTwin** target/inverse search (SSOT §246.9 L26779–26782). This part is only allowed after shared gates pass (SSOT L26714–26717; MP L4771).

**SCIENTIFIC RATIONALE**
The scientific claim of CulinaryState-RAG is not "an LLM answers cooking questions". The claim is that **state- and condition-compatible evidence retrieval, combined with an explicit, calibrated support cascade, reduces unsupported and infeasible claims at useful coverage compared with strong generic RAG** (RQ16-01/02/03/05/06/30; G16-EVID/CAL/DEC).

Three facts in the repo and the literature make this specific:
1. **Topical relevance is not the relevance this task needs.** Relevance here is cell identity (matrix × state × process × target × conditions).
   - Generic MS-MARCO rerankers *hurt*: bge-reranker-large ΔMRR −0.056 [−0.091, −0.017] (`reports/del4/retrieval_silver_v2_analysis.md`).
   - Structured slot retrieval dominates on silver: MRR 0.856 with oracle slots; hard-negative AUROC 0.975 with predicted slots (`reports/del4/rq1603_pilot_v1.md`).
2. **LLMs over-answer when context is insufficient** (Joren et al., ICLR 2025; Feng et al., ACL 2024; AbstentionBench 2025 preprint). So abstention must be a rule cascade over separately calibrated features, not generator self-confidence (`research/r_rag_confidence.md` Q5–Q6).
3. **The evidence is sparse, MNAR and concentrated.**
   - 17,978 ACTIVE rows, all E3, 0 human-verified.
   - 78% of rows come from two databases.
   - pH/moisture are UNKNOWN in 100% of rows, temperature in 67%, duration in 83% (ES-1.1 audit; `research/r_rag_confidence.md` §0.2).
   - So most real queries cannot reach DIRECT. The scientific value of the system is that it *says so* correctly (KNOWN UNKNOWNS, QUALITATIVE, ASK, ABSTAIN) without inventing values.

FlavorTwin's claim is narrower. It is **evidence-gated, state/process-aware inverse search with typed similarities and non-circular evaluation**. Static structural/co-occurrence pairing is already published work (FlavorGraph, KitcheNette, RecipeMind, FoodPuzzle, FlavourBench, Tagkopoulos 2026 preprint; `research/r_representation_flavortwin.md` Q8). Chemical similarity ≠ perceived flavour (SSOT L26767–26774).

**WHY NOW**
Not now as a whole. Step 36's *evaluated* form sits at the end of the DAG: it needs the Step 15 freeze, Step 08 lineage, the Step 19 Deep Gold and Steps 29–33 gates. Three parts are cheap and should start early, in parallel:
- **36.0:** audit the pre-spine prototype so nobody rebuilds it from scratch or mistakes it for "done".
- **36A schema work:** packet v2, the certainty profile and the canonical support enum. Earlier steps (03/04/07/08/09/15) must emit the fields these need. This is backward requirement propagation (§D).
- **36B benchmark protocol plus pilots P1/P2:** human labels are the binding constraint (`research/r_rag_confidence.md` §6). Authoring is the human long pole and can run alongside Steps 08–20. Locked-test items are pinned only after the Step 15 freeze.

Everything that makes a claim (36C locked ladder and calibration; 36D FlavorTwin) waits for its gates.

Required where confidence was MEDIUM/LOW on a material decision:
- retrieval-layer choice for a typed ledger;
- GraphRAG fit;
- conflict representation;

All of these were researched in this run (`research/r_rag_confidence.md`, `research/r_representation_flavortwin.md`, `research/r_eval_splits.md`, `research/r_l13e_identity.md`). The stop rule was met (brief §8 criteria 1, 2 and 5). What remains is empirical (pilots P1/P2), not bibliographic.

**RESEARCH FINDINGS** (cited; HIGH unless marked)

Retrieval and generation:
- **R1 Retrieval.** BM25 is a robust zero-shot baseline (BEIR, Thakur et al., NeurIPS 2021 D&B), and RRF suits incomparable scores (Cormack et al., SIGIR 2009).
  - Structured slot retrieval is primary for a typed ledger (repo silver MRR 0.856 oracle slots vs RRF 0.762 vs BM25 0.597).
  - Dense adds +0.005 [−0.006, +0.015] on top of structured, which is n.s.
  - Generic cross-encoders are negative. Late interaction (ColBERTv2) is unjustified at ~10^4–10^5 rows.
  - Confidence is MEDIUM for the project-specific numbers, because they are silver and templated with near-oracle slots.
- **R2 GraphRAG** (Edge et al. 2024) targets global sensemaking over an LLM-written index.
  - REJECT it as an evidence source (model memory ≠ evidence memory).
  - Curated graphs (food hierarchy, process family, lineage, mechanism) serve as retrieval *structure* only.
  - Vertical food-hierarchy expansion was promoted on silver (coverage 7.1%→20.3%, MAE Δ −0.026 [−0.035, −0.017]). Siblings were worse (+0.036) (`reports/del4/graph_expansion_v1_analysis.md`).
- **R3 SciFact/MultiVerS** (Wadden et al. EMNLP 2020; Findings NAACL 2022) belong in Step 09 extraction verification, not at runtime over structured rows. Runtime claim checking is AIS/ALCE-style attribution.
- **R4 Conflicts.** The knowledge-conflict taxonomy (Xu et al., EMNLP 2024) applies. The dominant type here is inter-context, and most apparent conflicts dissolve under harmonisation.
  - SSOT §241.5's 8-step harmonise-first workflow is the right design.
  - LLM debate/majority (MADAM-RAG, 2025, venue UNVERIFIED) is rejected (SSOT L42208–42218 "do not majority-vote blindly"; MP W12 L1915).
  - The repo detector is direction-only: INCREASE vs DECREASE.

Sufficiency, abstention and calibration:
- **R5 Sufficiency** is separately estimable (Joren et al., "Sufficient Context", ICLR 2025). Selective generation using it raises accuracy among answered items by ~2–10%. For structured rows, sufficiency is rule-derivable from the compatibility vector and must be validated on human labels. Confidence: MEDIUM for transfer.
- **R6 Selective prediction.** Use the risk–coverage frame (El-Yaniv & Wiener JMLR 2010), threshold bounds (Geifman & El-Yaniv 2017) and AURC/E-AURC (Geifman et al. ICLR 2019). Feature calibrators beat softmax under shift (Kamath et al. ACL 2020).
  - LLMs fail to abstain (Feng et al. ACL 2024; AbstentionBench arXiv 2506.09038, venue not listed).
  - So the generator never decides abstention. LLM self-confidence is a baseline only.
- **R7 Conformal methods.**
  - CQR (Romano et al. 2019) is for MODEL-rung intervals.
  - Conformal risk control (Angelopoulos et al., ICLR 2024) and conformal factuality back-off (Mohri & Hashimoto, ICML 2024) are for thresholds and precision back-off.
  - Guarantees are marginal and need exchangeability. Weighted conformal needs a likelihood ratio that is unavailable for food-, study- or process-cold shift (Tibshirani et al. 2019).
  - So cold-split coverage is reported **empirically only**. Confidence is LOW-MEDIUM on applicability at our n.
  - Repo precedent: conformal-90 coverage was 0.72–0.87 on cold splits (DEL-2; WORKLOG L117).
- **R8 Small-n calibration.** Use Platt/temperature (Guo et al. ICML 2017).
  - Isotonic overfits below ~1,000 samples (scikit-learn calibration docs).
  - Plug-in binned ECE is biased (Kumar et al. NeurIPS 2019).
  - The repo ECE uses equal-width bins only (`src/culinarystate/scoring/calibration.py`).
- **R9 Citation faithfulness.** Use ALCE citation recall/precision (Gao et al. EMNLP 2023), AIS (Rashkin et al. 2023) and FActScore (Min et al. EMNLP 2023). Numeric claims are checked *exactly* (value + row id). UCR (SSOT §245.7 L26645–26649) stays the headline. The repo template generator B5T reached 0/24 unsupported on silver.
- **R10 Certainty profile.** GRADE (Guyatt et al. BMJ 2008; Balshem et al. JCE 2011) rates certainty per outcome across separate domains.
  - Adopt its *domains*, not its RCT start-level arithmetic.
  - Add food-specific domains: basis, censoring, source-side imputation and lineage duplication.
  - Result: a 10-domain ordinal profile D1–D10. Domains are never multiplied and UNKNOWN is never coerced.

Benchmark sizing:
- **R11 Calibration and benchmark sizing** (arithmetic, stdlib, this run). Two-sided 95% Clopper–Pearson upper bounds on selective risk:

| n | errors | upper bound |
|---|---|---|
| 104 | 5 | ≤10.9% |
| 240 | 12 | ≤8.6% |
| 320 | 16 | ≤8.0% |
| 240 | 0 | ≤1.5% |
| 60 | 0 | ≤6.0% |

  - A McNemar paired 10 pp difference needs ≈155–233 items (`research/r_eval_splits.md` Q8).
  - So the **240-item locked tier is the minimum** for any headline paired claim. The 104 tier is descriptive. Per-rung guarantees at α=5% need several hundred labels *per rung*.

FlavorTwin:
- **R12 FlavorTwin.** The novelty space has narrowed in 2024–2026 (FoodPuzzle KDD 2025; FlavourBench 2026 preprint; Epicure 2026 preprints; Tac et al. 2026 preprint; Tagkopoulos et al. 2026 preprint; NotCo patent US10957424B1).
  - Still plausibly novel: evidence-gated, state/process-aware inverse search with typed per-notion similarities, null models and family-disjoint evaluation.
  - This must be re-checked before any paper. Confidence MEDIUM.
  - Ingredient-level sensory similarity is UNSUPPORTED: no public ingredient-level sensory labels were found, and the repo has no volatiles and no odour thresholds.

**ARCHITECTURE** (summary; full design in `parts/N_rag.md`)
Six-plane read model:
- SOURCE, RECIPE-SEMANTIC, SCIENTIFIC-EVIDENCE, STATE/EPISODE, MODEL and SIMULATION are kept separate.
- SSOT §232.3 keeps D^simulated separate (L25268–25272). §233.7 merges it into model memory; this card follows §232.3 (SSOT change request §F-1).

Pipeline:

```
C1 query/intent + slot parse (raw kept; slot confidences = D8)
  → C2 entity link (frozen BGE linker; unresolved stays unresolved)
  → C3/C4 state + history from event-sourced graph (current_state_version)
  → C5 goals/constraints (hard vs soft; no invented priorities)
  → C6 candidate generation:
       L1 structured slot→key lookup (PRIMARY)
       L2 vertical hierarchy expansion (food CHILD/PARENT; process SAME_FAMILY)
       L3 BM25 ∪ L4 dense (e5-large-v2) via RRF — recall FALLBACK only, never blended into L1 ranking
  → C7 compatibility vector (13 axes, categorical match types; UNKNOWN neutral-but-flagged; censoring/basis aware)
       + compatibility classifier ONLY if it beats L1-with-predicted-slots on HUMAN labels (RQ16-03)
  → R7 lineage dedup (Step-08 split_group / recipe OP-SPLIT) + §241.5 harmonise-first conflict clustering
  → C8 direct lookup | C9 MODEL rung (whitelisted G15 domains only; Step-27 IN_VALIDATION_DOMAIN only)
  → certainty profile D1–D10 per (query × outcome cell) + evidence status (frozen 3-value, separate)
  → cascade: DIRECT → INTERPOLATE → MODEL → QUALITATIVE → [ASK pre-empts when VOI>0] → ABSTAIN
       conflict_status ⟂ rung → REPORT_CONFLICT flag; precision cap = min(evidence precision, rung cap)
       per-rung thresholds from small Platt calibrators on a CALIBRATION partition (never isotonic <1k labels)
  → C10–C15 decision layer (feasibility before utility; diagnosis proposer→verifier; recovery evidence separate; Pareto, no global utility)
  → packet v2 (brief §27 + §257M header + additions) → C16 deterministic template (B5T) [+ optional local-LLM rephrase under enforcer]
  → C17 runtime claim ledger (claim_id → evidence ids/model output → claim_route → allowed precision) → UCR/citation metrics
  → C18 session update (observation overrides prediction on observable fields)
FlavorTwin (36D, later): target views → static baselines → typed per-notion similarity (Step 35) → process expansion only for
  supported candidates → evidence/OOD/constraint gate → Pareto candidates with §246.6 evidence classes; inverse design I0→I1 only
  under G15-INV / G15-12.
```

**DO**
1. Treat the DEL-4/DEL-5 code as a prototype to **re-evaluate** (36.0), not to rebuild and not to count as done.
2. Freeze **one canonical support enum** and one conflict-status enum, with a crosswalk to §242.6, §214.30, §246.6, §257A.14, MP AI7/AZ8 and the repo `evidence_class`. Do this in 36A, in coordination with Step 04.
3. Ship **packet schema v2** as JSON Schema. Every packet carries the §257M mandatory header (query ID, current state version, packet version, evidence class, known unknowns, claim/citation map, model version if used, confidence features, response mode) plus the §N.11 additions.
4. Replace the direction-only conflict detector with the **§241.5 harmonise-first workflow**, emitting conflict clusters with a harmonisation trace.
5. Keep **structured retrieval primary** and BM25+dense (RRF) as a recall fallback. Keep the generic cross-encoder **dropped** and retain that negative result.
6. Use a **non-scalar certainty profile** with per-decision Platt calibrators fitted only on an **independent calibration partition**.
7. Build the **human benchmark** (36B) per D-008 once approved:
   - dev / calibration / locked partitions (SSOT §257A.15 L28336);
   - locked ≥240 for headline paired claims;
   - items carry `split_group_id` and `evidence_cell_id`;
   - locked test sealed with hash and access log (MP AH13 L2961).
8. Run the SSOT ladder **B0–B7 exactly as §245.12** with the 9 one-at-a-time ablations, oracle cascades and robustness tests. Promote a module only if it beats the strongest simpler baseline beyond paired cluster-bootstrap uncertainty.
9. Enable the **MODEL rung only for (target, domain) pairs in a machine-readable G15 whitelist** derived from the §216.13 decision record. The whitelist is currently empty, so B6 ≡ B5 today and that is reported.
10. Pre-register all Step 36 thresholds (§A PASS GATE) before any locked-test access.
11. Keep FlavorTwin at the §246 boundary. Static FlavorTwin goes first; process-conditioned FlavorTwin is NEED_DATA.

**DO NOT**
- Do not let the generator LLM decide answer vs abstain, or emit numbers absent from the packet.
- Do not use LLM verbal confidence except as a baseline.
- Do not compute or show a single scalar confidence, and do not multiply domain scores (SSOT L26381; §49.x per `research/r_rag_confidence.md`).
- Do not use GraphRAG/LLM-written summaries or LLM-built KGs as evidence.
- Do not adjudicate conflicts by LLM vote.
- Do not calibrate on AI-assisted Gold (D-016/D-017; GOLD_PENDING_INDEPENDENT_IAA) or on templated silver queries. SSOT §242.3 L26399–26402 and invariant #14 require independent calibration data.
- Do not claim conformal guarantees under food-, process- or study-cold shift.
- Do not use simulated sessions (RQ16-14) or any synthetic/imputed item as a headline test (invariant #15).
- Do not tune prompts, thresholds or architecture on the locked test (§257P last RAG box; MP AH13).
- Do not surface simulator or model numbers outside the validated domain, or let imputed/simulated values masquerade as direct evidence (SSOT L26444).
- Do not quote RESTRICTED (A1 BBC, local-only) source text verbatim in shared outputs.
- Do not make any sensory-equivalence statement without sensory evidence (SSOT L26767–26774, L22552–22555).
- Do not expand FlavorTwin before the shared gates pass (SSOT L26714–26717).
- Do not reopen the frozen NER/linker (D-020).

**BASELINES**
- **System ladder (SSOT §245.12 exactly):** B0 LLM-only; B1 dense RAG; B2 BM25+dense RRF; B3 structured metadata; B4 state-aware; B5 state + compatibility/conflict packet; B6 + L15 fallback (whitelist only); B7 + calibrated recommend/ask/abstain.
- **Retrieval:** BM25; best dense (e5-large-v2); RRF; structured with oracle and with predicted slots; generic CE (control).
- **Confidence and abstention:**
  - always-answer RAG (RQ16-06 control);
  - scalar-threshold abstention on the current hand-weighted rank score;
  - LLM verbal confidence;
  - Joren-style sufficiency autorater (free-text only);
  - rule cascade without calibration.
- **Conflict:** majority vote / first hit (RQ16-22 control).
- **Decision:** NeverAsk / AskEverything vs VOIAsk (§245.10); RAG/LLM action list vs feasibility filter (RQ16-16).
- **Generator:** B5T deterministic template (current promoted) vs local LLM + enforcer (B5F+E).
- **FlavorTwin:** random, category, n_ij/IDF, ECFP-set, static text embedding, FlavorGraph-like vectors (licence check), LLM zero-shot/RAG, GISMo/LLM substitution (SSOT §246.8 L26775–26778; `research/r_representation_flavortwin.md` §3.2).

**METRICS**
- **Retrieval:** Recall@K, MRR, nDCG, and condition-compatible Recall@K (§245.6), per hard-negative type; support AUROC/F1.
- **Mode prediction:** macro-F1 over {DIRECT, INTERPOLATE, MODEL, QUALITATIVE, ASK, ABSTAIN} plus the REPORT_CONFLICT flag, with a confusion matrix and an asymmetric cost matrix (over-claim cost > under-claim cost).
- **Abstention:** precision/recall/F1 vs gold must-abstain; false-abstention rate; selective risk at fixed coverage (50/70/90%) with Clopper–Pearson bounds; RC curve, AURC, E-AURC.
- **Calibration:** Brier; ECE with equal-mass bins and a debiased estimator, plus bootstrap CI; reliability plots per decision.
- **Intervals:** coverage and width per split and per cluster, worst-cluster coverage (INTERPOLATE/MODEL).
- **Grounding:**
  - UCR, the headline (SSOT L26645–26649);
  - ALCE-style citation recall/precision per atomic claim (exact match for numeric claims; NLI/human for qualitative);
  - AIS human audit agreement;
  - precision-cap violations (target 0);
  - silent class upgrades (must be 0).
- **Decision:** Action R@K, feasibility violation rate, ASK quality vs number of questions.
- **Robustness:** paraphrase/unit invariance (§245.15).
- **Efficiency:** latency and cost per answer (§257B reporting item).
- **FlavorTwin:** Recall@K/MRR/nDCG, constraint satisfaction, abstention coverage–risk, diversity, per-notion components.

**LEAKAGE CONTROLS**
- **Recipe plane:** benchmark items are nested in recipe SPLIT_GROUP (07I-C OP-SPLIT). A Gold/benchmark recipe's SPLIT_GROUP is excluded from any tuning set (`research/r_eval_splits.md` R-2).
- **Evidence plane:** items carry `evidence_cell_id`. The calibration partition is lineage-disjoint from dev and locked (§242.3; `research/r_eval_splits.md` Q6).
- **MODEL fallback:** when evaluating the MODEL rung, the retrieval index and the model training data exclude held-out test evidence (L2 leakage; `research/r_eval_splits.md` §4).
- **Locked test:** sealed with a hash commitment and an access log, one read per confirmatory claim. Any second read needs H5 approval and is labelled exploratory (MP AH13 L2961; MP L139).
- **Anchoring:**
  - Gold answers and P1/P2 labels are authored **blind to system output** (`seen_system_output=false` recorded).
  - Identical-file and timestamp provenance checks run before a human gate counts (07H precedent: v3 files 11 s apart, NOT_COUNTED).
  - Choi et al. EMNLP 2024 found expert–LLM agreement rose 43.9%→71.5% when suggestions were shown (`research/r_eval_splits.md` Q7).
- **Templates:** templated silver queries (DEL-4) never enter the locked test. Paraphrase clusters and authoring session are cluster units for the bootstrap.
- **Independence:** endpoint-phrase leakage (SSOT L26495) is respected for state items. Retrieval dedups lineage copies so "5 copies ≠ 5 sources" (SSOT L25309).

**UNCERTAINTY / CONFIDENCE**
Overall step confidence is MEDIUM:
- Architecture: HIGH. SSOT, literature and repo negative results agree.
- Transfer of silver retrieval results to human questions with predicted slots: MEDIUM.
- Achieving calibrated per-rung guarantees: LOW, because label budget, not method, is binding.
- Frequency of genuine conflicts sufficient to evaluate G16-CONFLICT: LOW.
- FlavorTwin novelty: MEDIUM. FlavorTwin process-conditioned data: LOW (NEED_DATA).

Reported numbers carry paired cluster-bootstrap CIs with n_clusters, or a sign-flip permutation when there are fewer than about 20–30 clusters (`research/r_eval_splits.md` Q5).

**COMPUTE**
- CPU sufficient for all of 36.0–36C: rule cascade, BM25, structured lookup, compatibility, Platt calibrators, bootstrap evaluation (seconds to minutes on 128 cores), and the deterministic template generator.
- GPU helpful only for:
  - refreshing dense embeddings (e5-large-v2; previously run on the A100 per `reports/del4/retrieval_silver_v2_analysis.md`). About 18k rows is feasible on CPU, and the cached embeddings in `data/interim/embeddings` are reusable if the model hash matches.
  - an optional local LLM rephrase rung (B5F+E). This is unpromoted and not on the critical path.
- A100 unnecessary. It is not to be planned for, given VPN throughput of 13–90 KB/s (D-025). The shared server GPUs are off-limits (ctx.md).

**HUMAN REVIEW**
- D-008 approval: Kush + Parv, about 1 h each.
- P1 pair labelling: double-blind, about 6–10 h each (UNVERIFIED; 2–3 min/pair).
- P2 must-abstain authoring: about 8 h plus about 4 h second labelling.
- Locked benchmark authoring at the 320 tier: about 55–80 h total, split across Kush and Parv. This is UNVERIFIED (10–15 min per item including gold evidence ids), and pilots must log per-item time.
- Curated conflict labels: domain expert, about 5–10 h.
- AIS claim audit: about 100 claims, about 3–5 h each.
- Scientific claim review subset: double-annotated, shuffled outputs (MP AH14 L2969–2973), expert about 5–10 h.
- 36D (deferred): substitution-pair curation about 10 h each. A sensory panel is NEED_DATA (no resource).

Totals for 36.0–36C:
- Kush ≈ 45–65 h;
- Parv ≈ 45–65 h;
- expert-domain ≈ 10–20 h.

These are estimates only (brief §35). Deep Gold (Step 19) hours are **not** included.

**LICENCE / ACCESS**
- **Packet licence flags:** each cited source carries `licence_class`, `raw_redistribution_allowed` and `derived_redistribution_allowed` (`registry/recipe_source_usage_registry_v1.csv`; SSOT §250 L27526–27557).
  - A1 BBC is RESTRICTED/local-only: it can be cited by id and never quoted in shared answers.
  - Phenol-Explorer redistribution needs author permission (H2Q #5).
  - Food.com CC0 is uploader-declared and unverified.
  - FlavorGraph/FlavorDB is NC/DERIVED_ONLY, which affects any FlavorTwin release.
  - TASTEset licence is inconsistent (MIT vs LICENCE_UNVERIFIED).
- **Safety and allergens:** feasibility uses authority tables only (FSSAI/FSIS; MP L615, L3270). FlavorDB is never an allergen authority (S006 law).
- **Models:** licences and hashes of e5-large-v2, the BGE linker and any local LLM (qwen2.5 via Ollama used in DEL-5) must be recorded (UNVERIFIED here).
- **No external API services** may receive project data at runtime unless H2 approves. The deterministic template path needs none.

**PASS GATE** (PROPOSED_ONLY; operationalises G16-EVID/CONFLICT/CAL/TRANS/DEC/PROV/OOD; numbers are PROPOSED_PILOT, to be pre-registered in `experiments/EXP-*/card.md` before any locked-test access)
- **G36-A Compiler integrity (36A):**
  - 100% of packets validate against PKT v2;
  - 0 silent evidence-class upgrades;
  - 0 imputed/simulated/model values in DIRECT/INTERPOLATE sections;
  - every factual claim in RCL maps to an evidence id or an explicit model output (G16-PROV);
  - every conflict cluster has a harmonisation trace;
  - deterministic replay is byte-identical on two runs.
- **G36-B Benchmark validity (36B):**
  - D-008 approved;
  - provenance-validity check passes (no identical files, timestamps plausible, `seen_system_output=false`);
  - double-labelled subsets report raw agreement, κ/α, prevalence and PABAK where prevalence >0.9;
  - pre-registered agreement floor PROPOSED α/κ ≥ 0.67 for tentative and ≥ 0.80 for confirmatory use (`research/r_recipe_semantics_gold.md`);
  - locked tier achieved and reported (≥240 for headline paired claims);
  - seal hash recorded.
- **G36-RET (G16-EVID):** on human items with predicted slots, structured+fallback condition-compatible Recall@10 ≥ best simpler rung (B2 RRF). The paired cluster-bootstrap lower bound must be > 0, or the result non-inferior within δ_RET = 0.02. Per-hard-negative-type AUROC is reported.
- **G36-CONF (G16-CONFLICT):** on curated conflict cases, harmonise-first clustering F1 beats the majority/first-hit baseline (paired LB > 0). An audit sample shows 0 GENUINE conflicts collapsed silently.
- **G36-CAL (G16-CAL):**
  - calibrators are fitted only on the calibration partition of independent gold;
  - Brier, equal-mass and debiased ECE with CI are reported per decision;
  - the calibrated-cascade AURC is lower than the scalar-threshold baseline AURC at matched coverage, with the paired CI excluding 0;
  - cold-split coverage is reported empirically.
- **G36-ABST (RQ16-06, G15-7):**
  - selective-risk Clopper–Pearson upper bound ≤ α at the operating coverage (PROPOSED α = 0.10 overall at n ≥ 240);
  - abstention F1 on must-abstain items beats always-answer;
  - false-abstention rate ≤ pre-registered bound (PROPOSED ≤ 0.15 on DIRECT-regime items);
  - numeric UCR = 0 and precision-cap violations = 0 on locked.
- **G36-TRANS (G16-TRANS):** the MODEL rung is active only for whitelisted (target, domain) pairs. An empty whitelist is a valid PASS: B6 ≡ B5 and this is reported.
- **G36-DEC (G16-DEC):** B7 reduces unsupported or infeasible actions vs B5 and vs B2, with paired LB > 0. Coverage loss stays within a pre-registered bound (PROPOSED ≤ 10 pp).
- **G36-OOD (G16-OOD):** behaviour is reported on food-, process- and both-new strata (SSOT S4 abstention stratum; `research/r_eval_splits.md` Q1).
- **G36-LOCK:** §257P RAG block 8/8 ticked; access log shows one read per confirmatory claim.
- **G36-FT (G16-FT, 36D):** process conditioning beats static on a held-out process-sensitive task beyond CI, with no increase in OOD or constraint violations.

**FAIL ACTION** (forward failure paths; detail in §E)
- G36-A fails → fix the compiler; no evaluation is run.
- G36-RET fails (structured does not beat hybrid on human questions) → SSOT §249.2 stop rule: keep B2 as retriever and invest in slot parsing/linking (Steps 16–17), not rerankers. The negative result is recorded.
- G36-CAL fails → no calibrated-probability claims. Ship the rule cascade with empirical RC only, and acquire more independent gold (Step 19 DG-2→DG-3).
- G36-ABST over-claims → tighten the precision cap and rung predicates. If it over-abstains → report the trade-off and keep the simpler B5.
- G36-DEC fails → keep B5/B6.
- G36-FT fails → ship static FlavorTwin and say so.
- If most items are UNSUPPORTED → return to acquisition (Step 14 coverage map, fed by the 36 query log).

**FALLBACK**
- If 36C cannot be calibrated because labels are missing, Step 36 delivers B0–B5 (the SSOT "minimum course deliverable", L27657) with an uncalibrated but rule-transparent cascade.
- All confidence is reported as an ordinal profile, never as probabilities.
- If the human benchmark cannot reach 240 locked items, the 104 tier is reported as **descriptive only**, with no paired superiority claims.

**PARALLEL WORK**
- 36.0 now.
- 36A (schemas and specs) in parallel with Steps 08–15, developed against the ES-1.1 snapshot and re-pinned at the Step 15 freeze.
- 36B protocol and P1/P2 pilots in parallel with Steps 08–20 once D-008 is approved and 07I-C passes. Locked items wait for the Step 15 freeze.
- 36D static design in parallel with Step 35.
- L13E E13E-17/18 stay DEFERRED (36-H).

**NEXT IF PASS**
- Promote CulinaryState-RAG v1. Its claims are bounded by its achieved tier and gates.
- Release DATA-RETRIEVAL-BENCH / DATA-DECISION-BENCH per MP AX7, respecting licence tiers.
- Unlock 36D static FlavorTwin, then 36D process-conditioned only if G36-FT data exist.
- Write the CulinaryState-RAG paper unit (SSOT §248.2 L27430–27433).

**STOP FOR REVIEW**
Stop for review:
1. after 36.0 (prototype audit and enum/ladder rulings, which need H4 for the RCL- prefix and support enum);
2. after 36B pilots (P1/P2 results and agreement);
3. before the locked test is sealed (H5);
4. before any claim (H6).

- G16-EVID/CAL/DEC/PROV and the §257P final-claims checklist exist only here.
- It is also the consumer that justifies many earlier fields (§D). Remove it and those fields become outputs with no downstream consumer (brief §41).

**DEPENDENCIES**
- **HARD:**

- **Gates:**
  - HUMAN: D-008; P1/P2 labels; locked authoring; H4 enum/prefix; H5 seal; H6 claims.
  - DATA: independent gold; human-verified rows; conflict cases; volatiles for 36D.
  - RESEARCH: none blocking (pilots replace reading).
  - COMPUTE: CPU only.

**SCIENTIFIC QUESTION**
Does state- and condition-compatible evidence compilation, with a calibrated support cascade, reduce unsupported and infeasible claims at useful coverage compared with strong generic RAG? And is each added module's value distinguishable from zero under paired cluster uncertainty on cold strata?

**ENGINEERING QUESTION**
- Can packets be compiled deterministically and replayably, with full provenance, licence flags and a claim ledger, and with latency suitable for interaction?
- Can the cascade be operationalised with explicit, auditable rung predicates that never coerce UNKNOWN?

**KNOWN EVIDENCE**
R1–R12 above, plus the retained repo negative results:
- rerankers worse;
- dense+structured n.s.;
- siblings worse in hierarchy expansion;
- prompting ignores the precision cap;
- cold-split conformal under-coverage;
- persistence wins cold transition splits (DEL-2), so the MODEL rung currently has nothing to call.

**UNKNOWN / UNCERTAIN**
- Slot-parse accuracy on real user questions.
- Whether a compatibility classifier adds anything over structured retrieval with predicted slots (HARD AUROC 0.975 on silver leaves small headroom).
- Base rate of genuine conflicts after harmonisation.
- Achievable label budget and human minutes per item.
- Whether VOI-based ASK beats NeverAsk with few ambiguous scenarios.
- FlavorTwin novelty after Oct 2026.
- Whether any process-conditioned flavour target is acquirable.

**CONFIDENCE**
MEDIUM overall; HIGH for architecture; LOW for calibration claims and FlavorTwin process-conditioning.

**RESEARCH REQUIRED? / COMPLETED / RESULT**
- REQUIRED: yes, MEDIUM/LOW on retrieval, confidence, abstention, benchmark sizing and FlavorTwin novelty.
- COMPLETED: yes, in this run (`research/r_rag_confidence.md`, `r_eval_splits.md`, `r_representation_flavortwin.md`, `r_l13e_identity.md`).
- RESULT:
  - the architecture is stable and matches SSOT §241–§246;
  - changes are in operationalisation (rung predicates, ASK placement, CONFLICT orthogonal, certainty profile, packet v2, Platt-only, sizes);
  - more reading will not change the order. Pilots P1 (≈150–200 pairs) and P2 (≈100 must-abstain) are cheaper.

**ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED**

| Alternative | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Single scalar confidence | rejected | SSOT §242.1; hides the failing domain |
| LLM self-confidence for abstention | rejected; baseline only | — |
| Generic CE reranking | dropped | negative result kept |
| Dense-primary vector RAG | fallback only | — |
| GraphRAG / LLM KG as evidence | rejected | — |
| Isotonic / deep calibrators | rejected | below ~1k labels |
| Conformal guarantees under cold shift | rejected | report empirically |
| GRADE start-level arithmetic | rejected | domains adopted instead |
| LLM debate conflict resolution | rejected | — |
| Late interaction (ColBERTv2) | deferred | unless Step 13 serves full text at runtime |
| Full POMDP/RL decision layer | deferred | SSOT §243.11 L26511; §257A anti-creep L28480–28491 |
| LLM free generation as the primary generator | rejected | B5T template primary; LLM rephrase under enforcer optional |

**SIMPLE BASELINE / STRONG BASELINE / OPTIONAL ADVANCED MODEL**
- Simple: B2 BM25+dense RRF with always-answer, and the B5 rule cascade without calibration.
- Strong: B5 structured+compatibility+conflict packet with the B5T template; B7 with Platt per-decision calibrators and the VOI ASK rule.
- Optional advanced:
  - a small compatibility classifier on scientific hard negatives (RQ16-03);
  - conformal risk control for back-off thresholds;
  - a Joren-style sufficiency autorater for free text;
  - local-LLM rephrase under enforcer;
  - late interaction only with a full-text index.

**NEGATIVE CONTROLS**
- Shuffled evidence rows (packet with mismatched cells) → the system must fall to QUALITATIVE/ABSTAIN.
- Wrong-condition swap (same food/process, different T/t) → the compatibility filter must flag it.
- Must-abstain items (both-new stratum).
- Paraphrase/unit invariance.
- "Evidence sensitivity": adding a direct row must replace model-only mode (§245.15).
- A randomised-confidence calibrator → AURC must be worse.
- For FlavorTwin: frequency-preserving and Curveball nulls for any pairing claim (`research/r_l13e_identity.md`).

**ABLATIONS**
- The SSOT 9: state; quantity grounding; structured retrieval; compatibility; conflict/lineage; transition fallback; uncertainty/OOD gate; feasibility; provenance/claim ledger.
- Plus: hierarchy expansion on/off; dense fallback on/off; ASK on/off (NeverAsk); calibrator vs raw rule thresholds; template vs LLM rephrase.

**FAILURE MODES**
- Slot-parse failure silently mapping to the wrong cell → retriever semantic shortcut.
- Over-filtering under sparse evidence → false abstention (RQ16-06 main risk).
- Confidence theatre.
- Conflict collapse.
- Lineage duplication counted as replication.
- Transition overreach.
- Cascade error propagation (oracle vs predicted gap).
- Locked-test contamination via prompt tuning.
- Gold anchoring.
- Licence leakage of RESTRICTED text.
- Cost blow-up if LLM rephrase is used at scale.
- Course-deadline pressure to claim B7 on silver (WORKLOG W L5: presentation 25–26 Nov 2026).

**STOP CONDITION**
SSOT §249.2 applies:
- stop adding complexity if structured retrieval does not beat strong hybrid RAG;
- stop if confidence is uncalibrated under source shift;
- stop if L15 fallback raises UCR;
- stop if feasibility removes too many gold-valid actions;
- stop if process-conditioned FlavorTwin fails to beat static;
- stop if human verification cost exceeds the value of the feature.

Step 36 is *complete* when G36-A…G36-LOCK are each PASS or are recorded as a pre-registered negative/NEED_DATA verdict with its fallback shipped.

**DOWNSTREAM DEPENDENCIES**
- Publications: the CulinaryState-RAG paper (SSOT §248.2) and the FlavorTwin paper only if G36-FT passes.
- Releases: DATA-RETRIEVAL-BENCH, DATA-DECISION-BENCH, DATA-FLAVORTWIN-BENCH (MP AX7).
- The demo (≥8 scenarios; SSOT L27687–27694).
- The 36 query log feeds Step 14 coverage-driven acquisition (W10/W11; MP L1837–1890), which makes a feedback edge into the acquisition loop.

**ESTIMATED EFFORT**
- Agent days: 36.0 ≈ 2; 36A ≈ 6–8; 36B tooling ≈ 3; 36C ≈ 8–12; 36D ≈ 10–15 (deferred).
- Core total (36.0–36C) ≈ 19–25 agent days.
- Kush ≈ 45–65 h; Parv ≈ 45–65 h; expert-domain ≈ 10–20 h.
- All estimates are UNVERIFIED; pilots must log time.

**COMPUTE CLASS**
CPU sufficient; GPU helpful (dense re-embedding, optional LLM rephrase); A100 unnecessary.

**FINAL RECOMMENDATION**
MODIFY. Split into substeps 36.0/36A/36B/36C/36D with explicit gates; parallelise 36A/36B; DEFER 36D, with the process-conditioned part NEED_DATA.

**DECISION-MATRIX VALUE**
MODIFY

  - **36C.1** Re-run the retrieval ladder on human dev items with predicted slots (G36-RET).
  - **36C.2** RQ16-03 compatibility classifier vs structured with predicted slots, on P1 pairs. Promote only if the paired LB > 0 on cold strata.
  - **36C.3** Sufficiency: rule-derived from the compatibility vector, validated on P2.
  - **36C.4** Per-decision Platt calibrators (P(support), P(direct-correct), P(abstain-right)) on the calibration partition. Choose thresholds per rung by Clopper–Pearson selective-risk bounds or conformal risk control with UCR as loss. Guarantees are claimed on the random/exchangeable split only.
  - **36C.5** Cascade policy with rung predicates (`parts/N_rag.md` §N.13). ASK pre-empts by VOI (§243.8) and is tested NeverAsk vs AskAll vs VOIAsk.
  - **36C.6** C9 MODEL rung wired to `l15_fallback_whitelist_v1.csv` and the Step 27 domain flag. It is empty today, so it is disabled.
  - **36C.7** Decision layer: feasibility before utility; diagnosis proposer→verifier and recovery evidence kept separate (only if failure/recovery gold exists, else DEFER RQ16-18/19); C12 COMPARE = I0 evidence-only counterfactual (§214.7).
  - **36C.8** Locked B0–B7 ladder, 9 ablations, oracle cascades, robustness (one sealed read).
  - **36C.9 (36-H)** Historical-context retrieval (E13E-18): DEFER, because G13E-01/02 fail on the current corpus (`research/r_l13e_identity.md`).
- **DO NOT:** promote B7 on silver; use cold-split guarantees; use isotonic; let the LLM decide the rung.
- **OUTPUTS:** `reports/step36/{retrieval_human_v1,rq1603_human_v1,calibration_v1,cascade_rc_v1,ladder_B0_B7_locked_v1,ablations_v1,oracle_cascade_v1,robustness_v1}.md`; `reports/step36/step36c_gate_result.json`.
- **BASELINES / METRICS:** see §A.
- **PASS GATE:** G36-RET, G36-CONF, G36-CAL, G36-ABST, G36-TRANS, G36-DEC, G36-OOD, G36-LOCK.
- **FAIL ACTION / FALLBACK:** see §A and §E.
- **HARD DEPS:** 15, 08, 09, 07I-C, 19 (DG-2), 36A, 36B. **SOFT DEPS:** 16–18, 23, 24/27, 29–34.
- **HUMAN:** AIS audit and claim review. **COMPUTE:** CPU (GPU helpful for re-embedding). **EFFORT:** about 8–12 agent days.
- **REC:** MODIFY. **DM:** MODIFY.

### 36D — FlavorTwin (later): static → process-conditioned → inverse design
- **STATUS:** NOT STARTED.
- **GOAL:** target → candidate (ingredient + state + process + conditions) search over the shared core. Each candidate carries per-notion similarity components and a §246.6 evidence class. There is no universal scalar.
- **DO (when unlocked):**
  - **36D.1** Static FlavorTwin, after Step 35 delivers the typed similarity registry: mandatory static baselines (§246.8); evidence classes; abstention coverage–risk; family-disjoint evaluation; null models for pairing claims.
  - **36D.2** Process-conditioned FlavorTwin, **NEED_DATA**. It needs volatile/key-odorant before/after evidence (Steps 11–14) or validated transitions (Steps 27/33). G36-FT is then tested.
  - **36D.3** Inverse design (Claim F) is housed here, because it has no other spine home (`notes/ssot_l15b.md` §9 item 10).
    - I0 counterfactual comparison is shared with 36C COMPARE.
    - I1 grid/random feasible search over (T, t) runs only inside C_safe (SSOT L21628–21636).
    - It is blocked by G15-INV/G15-12 until forward gates pass.
    - It uses the IDT schema (the union of §216.5 and §214.44 fields).
  - **36D.4** Cultural prior (E13E-17; §279.6): DEFER.
- **DO NOT:** claim sensory equivalence; train and evaluate on co-occurrence (circular, §133.2); use KGE ALTERNATIVE_TO as gold.
- **OUTPUTS:** `reports/step36/flavortwin_static_v1.md`; `benchmark/flavortwin/*`; `ledgers/schemas/IDT.schema.json` (deferred).
- **PASS GATE:** G36-FT; §257P FlavorTwin block (5 boxes); G15-INV for 36D.3.
- **FAIL ACTION:** ship static FlavorTwin with evidence gating, and say so (SSOT §249.2).
- **HUMAN:** substitution-pair labels; a sensory study is NEED_DATA/DEFER (RQ16-27).
- **COMPUTE:** CPU sufficient for static; GPU helpful only for optional learned rungs inherited from Step 35.
- **LICENCE:** FlavorGraph/FlavorDB NC/DERIVED_ONLY; FooDB CC BY-NC; VCF commercial.
- **REC:** DEFER (process-conditioned = NEED_DATA). **DM:** DEFER.
