## K.2 Target definitions

| Target | Definition | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| **T1 retention factor RF** | after/before **on the source's stated basis**: TRUE retention (yield-corrected, Bognár), APPARENT, or USDA %TR/%AR undisclosed (RT-004) | Never merge definitions without harmonisation (SSOT L16632). `retention_definition` is a mandatory covariate or stratum. RF>1 is legitimate and never clipped (MP AM2 L3584; SSOT L20242). The Step-07 "fraction > 1 INVALID" rule must be verified to apply to bare fractions only (ssot_l15a C9) |
| **log retention** `ln RF` | Separate field `log_retention_factor` (D-018), distinct from `log_fold_change` | Secondary metric scale for ratio targets (TB L14). Never computed from censored values |
| **log fold change** `ln((c_after+ε)/(c_before+ε))` | For compound targets with before/after concentrations (PE only today: 3,870 delta rows) | ε must be declared. Only for uncensored values |
| **T2 yield / weight-change factor** | food mass after/before (Bognár 496 rows; USDA Cooking Yields R2 on disk, not ingested) | Also a covariate for true vs apparent retention. Not an independent target when attached from shared yield sources (PE: 103 yield records) |
| **Direction / ordinal** | Dead band ±δ, `[PROPOSED-PILOT]` ±10% (SSOT L16647) | δ must be declared as relative-on-RF (`|RF−1|≤δ`) before use; the SSOT is ambiguous (ssot_l14 §9 #19). Ordinal cut-points per target are pre-registered |
| **Censored observation** | `value_status ∈ {DETECTED, NON_DETECT, BELOW_LOD, BELOW_LOQ, ABOVE_CAP(GT_CAP), CENSORED_UNKNOWN, NOT_REPORTED, TRUE_ZERO}` + limit | TRUE_ZERO is missing from the CS registry and must be added (Step 03/05). Never substitute zero, mean, LOD/2 or a bound as truth (SSOT §222.2 L23961) |
| **Kinetic targets (D-C)** | ln(C/C0) per timepoint; k_ref, Ea per matrix class with CI | Only from K1/K2 series (Step 32) |

Each SVAR also needs `delta_semantics ∈ {ADDITIVE, RATIO_RETENTION, LOG_FOLD, CATEGORICAL, ORDINAL, NOT_TRANSITIONABLE}` and `bounds_type` (look-ahead to Step 03; ssot_l15a §10).

## K.4 Model families: when each is justified

| Family | Justified when | Not justified when | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Means / lookups (D0–D2, D4) | Always (the floor) | — | SSOT L18292–18336 |
| Hierarchical / mixed effects (D3-full) | Multi-source, nested food/process/target structure, study effects, few hundred independent units, censoring | Single-cell questions with direct evidence (use D4) | Karamcheti et al. 2025, Food Microbiol 128:104731: study variance > strain variance; SSOT §211.21 |
| Regularised linear (D3-R) | Sanity floor with side features | — | SSOT §209.6 |
| GBDT (D5) | ≥ low thousands of rows per source with informative features. Cold gain shown only under grouped tests | Gains appear only on random/pair splits (DEL-2 USDA/PE) | Grinsztajn 2022; McElfresh 2023; TabArena 2025 (IID only) |
| TabPFN (D6) | ≤10k rows, ≤500 features; CPU OK; comparator | Production or headline dependence; grouped-shift claims (vendor-only evidence) | Hollmann et al., Nature 637:319 (2025): random splits only |
| GP | Small numeric (log t, 1/T) interpolation within the PE subset or a focused system | Cold matrices (no meaningful kernel); MTGP transfer cancels in block designs | Bonilla et al. 2007 |
| Completion: MF / FM / BPMF / tensor (D7) | A well-defined matrix view; side features available for cold rows/columns; must beat D3-full/D5/D6 cold | Pure-ID MF for cold entities; density ~0.3% with no side information (PE D7≡D1) | Rendle 2010; Simm et al. 2015; SSOT §221 |
| Multi-task | Implemented as shared random effects (D3-full) or latent factors (D7) | A separate neural multitask net before D0–D7 | SSOT §200.7, §209.17 |
| Set / graph neural transitions | Compound-level concentration data exist (S4/S5) and D0–D7 have been decided | Today: presence-only compounds, no concentrations | SSOT §200.2; L16407 "Do not start here" |
| Kinetics (D8) | K1 (rate) / K2 (Arrhenius) series, within-study fits first | Aggregates without T,t (never estimate Ea from them; SSOT L19790) | SSOT §210–211 |
| Hybrid (D9) | D8 credible (G15-4) and time-resolved data; sequential fitting | Before D8 passes; joint fitting as the first hybrid | SSOT L24977, §211.45; von Stosch et al. 2014 |
| Neural ODE / CDE / UDE (D11) | Dense trajectories in a focused system | Endpoint data (SSOT §229.6 "What not to do") | Chen 2018; Kidger 2020; Rackauckas 2020 |
| Deep tabular (FT-Transformer, TabM, RealMLP) | Not a headline at this n | IID-only evidence; n_eff ~10² | Gorishniy 2021/2025; TabArena |
| PINN on aggregates | Never | No governing state for endpoint aggregates | SSOT §201.12 |

**Per-source modelling first; pooling is tested.**
- USDA + Bognár on shared nutrients: pooling is a cross-source transfer diagnostic (S-7 DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY; overlap only 67–249 cells).
- PE has zero target overlap with the other two, so it joins only through target-class random effects.
- Bognár process-disjoint is degenerate (7 signatures) and is never a headline.

## K.5 Sparsity and MNAR handling

1. **Mandatory artifact (Step 15).** Observed tensor + observation mask + metadata tensor W (tier, study, platform, n, LOD, yield, verification) + cold-start split registry (SSOT §229.3, L24987–25001).
2. **Evaluation.**
   - The §221.18 9-item protocol (L23911–23919): masked-real-cell; cold food/process/compound/pair; study-disjoint; platform/matrix stratification; calibration; frequency buckets.
   - The §222.10 7-item anti-inflation report (L24052–24060).
   - "Masked-real-cell" masking is **structured** (whole cells, grouped by lineage), never MCAR row masking.
3. **Propensity model e(x).**
   - Covariates: food popularity, target class, process, study year, platform, source type (SSOT §220.5).
   - It requires the **propensity universe**, meaning metadata for discovered-but-unextracted papers (Step 13, look-ahead LA-14).
   - Until then, DEL-2's marginal-frequency propensity is labelled "proxy".
   - IPS is clipped. DR is `[HYPOTHESIS]`. Positivity/overlap is reported (MP AM4).
   - It is a sensitivity analysis only, never a headline. "Propensity weighting does not license random row splits" (SSOT L23666).
4. **Missing covariates vs missing targets.**
   - Covariates may be imputed inside training folds, with masks retained.
   - Targets are never filled for evaluation.
   - Imputed targets are training-only class `I` with inflated noise (SSOT §222.9). Tier crosswalk at Step 04.
5. **Completed cells.** IMPUTED/MODEL-ESTIMATED, never evidence or citations (SSOT L23925–23937). Step 36 exposes them as MODEL_ESTIMATED_MATCH (RQ16-21).
6. **Frozen rule.** Synthetic or imputed targets never enter test or calibration (SSOT §223.14 L24249–24255; G15-10).

## K.6 Censoring

- Current DEL-2 training at bound 0.975 is single-value imputation. It conflicts with SSOT §201.9 (L16705), §222.5 (L23998) and the repo's own state contract L40.
- **Architecture:**
  - Training arms: (i) legacy bound (continuity); (ii) interval / Tobit likelihood (native in D3-full; AFT or interval objective for GBDT, tool availability UNVERIFIED); (iii) drop-censored sensitivity.
  - Evaluation: censor-aware MAE plus **separate censored and uncensored strata**.
- **Drafter's inference (from the DEL-2 table).** USDA matrix-disjoint D0 has median AE 0.0, and 37% of USDA rows are GT_CAP. So the cold-split advantage of persistence may be partly a cap artefact (UNVERIFIED magnitude). The stratified report decides it.
- Cap semantics: USDA "values >100 reported as 100" (r_evidence_model) supports GT_CAP. The Bognár "1.00" cap justification is UNVERIFIED. An expert check is assigned to Step 29.

---

## K.7 Uncertainty, conformal and calibration

- **Four uncertainty types are kept separate:** aleatoric, epistemic, evidence-distance/OOD, and kinetic-parameter (SSOT L18490–18499).
- **Group-disjoint calibration.**
  - Calibration partitions are group-disjoint in the same family as the test split they serve, and lineage-disjoint from train and test.
  - Use group-level repeated subsampling or CV+ for hierarchical data (Dunn, Wasserman & Ramdas, JASA 2023).
  - Use CQR for heteroscedastic targets (Romano et al. 2019).
  - Weighted conformal only as an experiment: it needs a likelihood ratio that is unavailable under cold-group shift (Tibshirani et al. 2019; Barber et al., Ann. Statist. 2023).
- **Reporting.**
  - Empirical coverage and width per split and **worst-cluster coverage** (WILDS-style).
  - Always labelled "empirical" (MP AH4).
  - Current reality: 0.72–0.87 at nominal 0.90 on cold splits (WORKLOG S017).
- **Coverage floor rule.**
  - A model may enter the Step-36 MODEL rung for a (target, domain) only if empirical coverage ≥ c_floor on the matching cold split. c_floor is PROPOSED_PILOT (0.85 at nominal 0.90) in `registry/phase_g_preregistration_v1.csv`.
  - Otherwise the route downgrades to QUALITATIVE/ABSTAIN rather than silently widening intervals.
- **G15-6 (real, study-disjoint calibration)** is feasible only on PE today.
- **Calibrators.** Only Platt/logistic with 1–6 features below ~1,000 labels; never isotonic (r_rag_confidence).
- **Rollout.** One-step coverage ≠ trajectory coverage (SSOT L20194). Coverage is reported by horizon.

---

## K.8 Evaluation protocol (Phase-G wide)

- **Splits (claim-first, r_eval_splits):**
  - TB S-1 random: reference only.
  - S-2 pair-holdout with C-class: compositional; secondary headline.
  - S-3 matrix-disjoint and S-4 process-disjoint: **primary cold criterion per TB §6**.
  - S-5 food-group-disjoint.
  - S-6 lineage-component-disjoint: PE-only.
  - S-7 source-disjoint: DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY.
  - Both-new: abstention stratum.
  - Condition-OOD: within-study blocking; NEED_DATA for cooking.
  - Matrix-OOD: Step 27/32 only.
  - Platform-disjoint: deferred (no data).
- **Headline conflict resolution.**
  - The SSOT says the headline is pair-holdout + study-disjoint (§202.3 L16898–16900). TB says min(S-2..S-5) with support only on S-3/S-4.
  - **TB's stricter pre-registered criterion is kept as primary.** Switching to pair-holdout now would be post-hoc weakening, because DEL-2 already showed D5 winning pair-holdout on USDA and Bognár.
  - Pair-holdout is reported as the SSOT secondary headline.
- **Statistics.**
  - Paired cluster bootstrap of differences (B≥10k) over the unit of independence. Cluster sign-flip permutation when there are fewer than ~20–30 clusters (Cameron et al. 2008).
  - No fold-SE CIs (Bates et al. 2023).
  - Nested grouped tuning (Cawley & Talbot 2010).
  - ≥5 seeds for stochastic learners.
  - Holm for confirmatory tests, BH for exploratory ones.
  - Margin-δ promotion (MP AM5).
  - Sealed test hash plus access log.
  - n_clusters printed with every number.
  - K_min clusters for any headline split (PROPOSED 10), else DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY.
- **Prior exposure.** All 17,978 E3 rows were inspected by DEL-2. Phase-G results on them are pre-registered re-analyses. Fresh confirmatory evidence comes only from rows first sealed at Step 15.
- **Shortcut controls (SSOT §199.10, §202.4):** source-family-only, study-ID-only, matrix-ID-only, basis-only, conditions-only and (when it exists) platform-only.
- **Label-noise ceiling.** Same-cell cross-source disagreement: USDA↔Bognár MAE 0.075–0.083 on 67 cells (`reports/del2/cross_source_v1.md`).

---

## K.9 Physics and condition features (Step 31)

- **31a (generic, before kinetics).**
  - Features: log(1+t), 1/T_K, Ω at a pre-declared 3-value Ea grid taken from Step-24 literature rows, time above threshold, heat mode, water-contact proxy, basis and yield flags.
  - Ablation arms A1/A3/A4/A5 (SSOT §215.56) on identical rows with measured conditions, plus a missing-indicator arm and a monotone-constraint arm.
  - Splits: condition-OOD within study and process-family-disjoint.
  - **Cooking vs storage strata are reported separately**, because PE series are mostly storage.
- **31b (after Step 32).** Ω from fitted (k_ref, Ea) posteriors. This is the multi-fidelity bridge (SSOT L19794–19804).
- **Ordering conflict.** §215.71 (features before kinetics) vs §216.7 (kinetic fits before features). It is resolved by the 31a/31b split (SCR-G-4).
- **Hard human gate.** A valid Step-07 condition audit (packet v4) and the fix for the months→seconds bug.

---

## K.10 Kinetics (Step 32), single-system machinery in Step 26a

- **System.** SIM-AA-1, ascorbic acid in vegetables under water or steam heating at 60–100 °C. Pre-registered fallback: SIM-CHL-1 (r_simulator_vv). Acrylamide and Maillard are RESEARCH_ONLY second systems, after Step 27 PASS.
- **Fitting (shared library 26a).**
  - Within-study first.
  - Global reference-T Arrhenius, hierarchical log k with matrix-class and study effects.
  - Censored likelihood.
  - Profile likelihood and study bootstrap.
  - LOTO and LOSO cross-validation.
  - Model selection by AICc **plus** held-out fit.
  - Degradation + leaching where water is assayed.
- **Step 32 content.**
  - The K0–K6 ablation (SSOT §215.57) on the downstream study-disjoint test, against Step 30/31.
  - Choice of primary model form by held-out fit.
  - G15-4 record.
- **Data gate.** Census quotas: ≥30 K1+ series from ≥10 groups and ≥3 K2-design groups (PROPOSED). Zero such series exist today, so Step 32 is **NEED_DATA**.

---

## K.11 Hybrid (Step 33)

- **Three arms on identical rows:** mechanistic (Step-32 K4 or the validated SIM-AA-1) / best non-kinetic ML (Step 30/31) / sequential hybrid (endpoint residual first; multiplicative positive correction).
- **Diagnostics:** residual-off ablation, ‖f_NN‖/‖f_mech‖, and the semigroup test (G15-8).
- **E7 arm**, only if Step 27 passed:
  - ratio sweep 0–5×;
  - matched-volume randomized simulator control;
  - real-n learning curve;
  - calibration-leakage audit;
  - pretraining variability wider than the real training range (Read et al. 2019).
- **Gate.** G15-HYB (beats **both** arms) and G15-5.
- **Out of scope.** The reaction-network arm, which belongs to a Step-28 simulator-recovery study (SSOT L21211).

---

## K.12 Rollout and trust horizon (Step 34)

- **34a (feasible now): composition consistency.**
  - Chain one-step predictions over composite multi-step rows: USDA 1,429 and PE 195.
  - Compare against the composite lookup and persistence.
  - **First check whether USDA multi-step factors are themselves multiplicative derivations (circularity).** If they are, use PE only.
  - This tests G15-8. It does not establish a horizon.
- **34b (NEED_DATA).**
  - H_trust = max k such that Coverage(k) ≥ c_min, E(k) ≤ ε_max and OOD(k) ≤ τ (SSOT L20556–20566).
  - c_min, ε_max and τ are pre-registered and calibrated on held-out calibration sequences, separate from test sequences.
  - Quantitative R2 only for the focused system with staged measurements.
  - R0/R1 only on Step-19 blind Gold trajectories.
  - **A D-D pass licenses R0/R1 only (SCR-G-1).**
- **Baselines.** M0, M1 and the symbolic deterministic updater + retrieval loop (SSOT L20509–20535). Learned M3–M6 only with order-labelled sequences.
- **34c rollout abstention.** Stop or downgrade when any of these hold: evidence distance > τ, width > ε_max, a constraint violation, k > H_trust, or an inferred (not observed) input state. Consumed by the Step-36 cascade.

---

## K.13 Is the order bootstrap → tabular → physics → kinetics → hybrid → rollout right?

**Verdict: yes in principle, with five corrections.** It is the SSOT's own order (§215.71 L22707–22722; §229.2 L24924–24981; "sparse-data structure before neural dynamics", L18545), and DEL-2 empirically supports exhausting the simple rungs first.

**Corrections:**
1. **29/30 are not downstream of Phases D–F.**
   - They depend on 08 + 15 only, so they move earlier and run in parallel with C–F.
   - Step 15 should allow a stratum-wise freeze (DATA-EVIDENCE v1-E3) so that V0 can run before acquisition completes.
2. **31 splits into 31a and 31b.**
   - 31a, generic features, is an ablation inside the Step-30 harness before kinetics.
   - 31b, fitted-parameter features, comes after 32.
3. **Kinetic machinery is a hidden prerequisite of Step 26.**
   - It moves to 26a.
   - Step 32 becomes the cross-study K0–K6 ablation and must reuse 24/25/26a parameters.
4. **32–34b are data-gated.**
   - The critical path through Phase G runs through acquisition (Steps 10–14: K2 series, staged sequences) and Step 19 Gold, not through modelling.
   - Per §215.70, the response to the current collapse is acquisition.
5. **34a is a cheap, legitimate early test**, runnable after 30.

**Effective DAG:**

```text
08 ─┬─> 15(E3 stratum) ─> 29 ─> 30 ─┬─> 31a ──────────────┐
    │                               ├─> 34a                │
    │                               └─> 36.C9 (provisional) │
10–14 (K2, staged) ─> 15(D-C stratum) ─┐                    │
24/25 ─> 26a ─> 26 ─> 27 ──────────────┼─> 32 ─> 31b        │
                                       │        └─> 33 <────┘
18/19 (Gold trajectories) ──────────────────────────> 34b <── 33
                                                       └─> 34c ─> 36
```

# L. REPRESENTATION / SIMILARITY ARCHITECTURE

## L.1 Verdict
The SSOT design (L12 §§174–183, L13 §§186–194, §246) is right in substance: fingerprints/explicit statistics first,
circularity ban, confound audits, no universal flavour scalar, gated learned rungs. Five things must change in the
execution plan:
1. **Placement**: explicit rungs run as a parallel CPU lane, not after Phase G (SSOT L169 "CORE EXECUTION PRIORITY";
   L27732 "PARALLEL"; MP L237). Learned and process-conditioned rungs stay late.
2. **De-duplication**: L12 threads T8/T9 (process kinetics, reaction-graph ODEs; SSOT L10905–10960) are the same work as
   Steps 29–34 → homed there; Step 35 consumes only promoted outputs (35f). §216.10 (L22967–22977) already forbids
   29–34 depending on learned z_m/z_i.
3. **Gate rewrite**: G3/G4/G7 are defined on GS-LF/Keller/ingredient sensory labels (L10796–10900) that the repo does
   not have and has marked out of scope (RESOURCE_GAP_MAP L19). They must be re-scoped to available tasks and
   thresholds pre-registered (G35-* gates) — or a human decision acquires licensed labels.
4. **Typed registry**: the repo has 21 SIM definitions (`registry/ssot15_similarity_registry.csv`) but no notion-level
   null/eval/split/domain/licence fields; brief §24 requires nine notions. → `registry/similarity_registry_v2.csv`.
5. **Split groups**: recipe-level evaluation needs the recall-oriented `split_group_id` from 07I-C (the SSOT
   `duplicate_group_id` in the repo is exact-only; §191.3 L14782–14785 requires near-duplicates in one group).

## L.2 The ladder (molecule → ingredient → recipe → cuisine)
```
LEVEL        EXPLICIT (35a–35d, CPU, early lane)                       GATED / LATE
molecule     E0 identity · E2 ECFP/Morgan Tanimoto · E3 descriptors      E4 graph emb · E5 pretrained · E7 multi-view (35g)
ingredient   E0 n_ij · E1 Jaccard/Ochiai/IDF · E2 kernel-mean/best-match  E6 DeepSets/attention/SetTransformer (35g)
             · E3 descriptor agg · OT ablation · tiered x_ij               OAV-weighted (NEED_DATA) · E8 process-cond (35f)
ingr.-state  —                                                           Δ-profile similarity from EVD / validated transitions (35f)
recipe       R0 incidence · R2-explicit TF-IDF · R1 mean explicit z_i ·    R4–R7 set models, R8 process/graph, R9 (35g, after 16–20)
             R3 quantity (CQPO subset) · frequency-only · kNN memorise
cuisine      C0 prevalence · C1 specificity/TF-IDF · C2 motifs ·           C3–C8 learned/distributional (35g)
             §85 fingerprint · C3-explicit mean recipe vector
```
Order inside the step: 35.0 → {35a, 35b, 35c, 35d, 35-E in parallel} → 35e → 35h(v1) ; later 35f → 35h(v2) ; 35g only on
explicit failure evidence + non-circular target.

## L.3 Substeps (fully specified)

### 35.0 Pre-registration and contract intake
- Inputs: Step 04 registry v2 schema; 07I-C `recipe_split_groups_v1` (or conservative fallback grouping); Step 06
  licence classes; this card.
- Do: write `reports/step35/preregistration_v1.md`: claims list (claim_id → primary metric × split × task family),
  multiplicity families (Holm confirmatory, BH exploratory), seeds (≥5) × folds (≥5), δ margins†, k (top-k removal),
  α (frequency weight), β (negative sampler), kNN k, minimum cuisine class support (≥100 recipes† and ≥3 sources† for
  source-disjoint claims), cardinality-slope bound (|ρ|≤0.3†), sealed-test access rules. Hash it.
- Outputs: preregistration + sha256; split manifests (`registry/splits/split_mol_scaffold_v1.json`,
  `split_mol_cluster_v1.json`, `split_ing_cluster_v1.json`, `split_recipe_group_v1.json`,
  `split_cuisine_holdout_v1.json`) with leakage audits.
- Gate **G35-PRE** + **G35-0** (see L.5). Human: Kush+Parv sign-off (~3 h each). Compute: CPU minutes.

### 35a Molecule features and leaderboard
- Inputs: MOL (1,726; InChIKey, SMILES, CACTVS-881, 6 descriptors); KGE MOL_HAS_TASTE (1,145 edges; licence per source
  to be confirmed — WORKLOG L600 records removal of unlicensed taste sources); odour labels only if licensed (pyrfume
  repo MIT at repo level, per-dataset terms UNVERIFIED this run).
- Do: compute ECFP4/Morgan r2 2048 bit (SIM-06 frozen) **and** count; FCFP; MACCS; RDKit2D (rdkit pinned); scaffolds
  (Murcko); Butina clusters. Freeze molecule splits (scaffold, cluster) with InChIKey full + connectivity-layer audit
  (70% stereo-undefined).
- Baselines: label prior; kNN-Tanimoto; ECFP4-count+LightGBM (**reference**, SSOT G2 L10766); ECFP-bit+RF;
  logistic/ridge; PubChem-881+LightGBM; RDKit2D+LightGBM; TabPFN (optional CPU comparator); OpenPOM MPNN reproduction
  only if odour tasks licensed (L11036).
- Tasks: taste class prediction (ChemTastesDB-type labels); odour descriptors (only if licensed); structural retrieval
  sanity (scaffold recovery).
- Metrics: macro AUROC/AUPRC, per-label F1, ECE/Brier, OOD gap (random − scaffold); paired cluster bootstrap over
  scaffold clusters.
- Gate: reference frozen (G2); a learned encoder can only be considered in 35g (G3/G4 re-scoped: "beats reference on ≥2
  available tasks under scaffold AND cluster splits with lower CI of Δ > 0.01 AUROC / 0.02 AUPRC (SSOT proposed)").
- Output: `ledgers/representation/molecule_fingerprints_v1.parquet`, `reports/step35/molecule_leaderboard_v1.md`.
- Compute: CPU minutes. Human: rdkit approval; licence decisions.

### 35b Ingredient chemical profile and aggregator ablation
- Inputs: IMAP (313 ING; 31,334 PRESENCE from FlavorGraph DERIVED_ONLY; 219 MEASURED_CONCENTRATION polyphenols; 419
  PROCESS_CHANGE), ING/ALIAS, 35a features.
- Do: build tiered `x_ij` = {tier ∈ PRESENCE | MEASURED_CONC | THRESHOLD | OAV_DERIVED, value or UNKNOWN, unit
  (case-normalised), basis (fresh/dry/per-volume/edible portion), matrix, state_id/form, study_id, source_family,
  licence_scope, evidence_ids}; OAV_DERIVED only when concentration and threshold share a compatible matrix (currently
  0 rows → NEED_DATA). Per-ingredient coverage record {n_compounds, n_sources, n_measured, coverage_class}.
- Arms: E0 n_ij; E1 Jaccard, Ochiai, IDF-overlap, null percentile; E2 kernel-mean Tanimoto, symmetrised best-match,
  top-k mean; E3 descriptor-space mean; OT (balanced) as one ablation arm; bag-of-compounds+LightGBM for supervised
  proxies.
- Tasks (non-circular): held-out recipe co-occurrence completion with family-disjoint splits (chemistry → held-out
  co-occurrence is "acceptable" per L8476–8482); ingredient category prediction (proxy, flagged); raw-vs-processed
  discrimination only in 35f.
- Diagnostics: cardinality slope ρ(score, |F_i|·|F_j|) per arm; profile-size-stratified metrics; 10–50% compound
  dropout; shuffled-compound and odourless-only controls; performance-vs-coverage regression.
- Gate: **G35-COV**; aggregator "promotion" per §183.3 (simplest within uncertainty kept). G7 sensory clause =
  DATA-BLOCKED (recorded, not waived).
- Output: `ledgers/representation/ingredient_profile_xij_v1.parquet`, `ingredient_profile_coverage_v1.parquet`,
  `reports/step35/ingredient_aggregator_ablation_v1.md`. Compute: CPU (313×313 pairs trivially; 5,387 when crosswalks
  grow).

### 35c Recipe explicit rungs (R0–R3)
- Inputs: recipe_base_v1 (612,782), 07I-C split groups, ING canonical links, vocab frequency table, CQPO quantities where
  present (Food.com/A1), source usage registry.
- Rungs: R0 binary incidence (Jaccard/cosine); R2-explicit TF-IDF incidence (z_i-free; resolves the SSOT R2 ambiguity
  L13782 vs L14738); R1 mean of explicit 35b z_i (only 313 profiled ING → coverage-limited, labelled); R3 quantity-
  weighted (mass-grounded shares; masked missing) on the quantity-rich subset; frequency-only shortcut; kNN memorisation
  baseline (nearest recipe by IDF-Jaccard across the split); LightGBM/logistic over R0/R2 for supervised tasks.
- Task families (≥2, §191.2): masked-ingredient recovery; partial-recipe completion; cross-source duplicate/identity
  retrieval (scored against 07I-C labels); cross-view retrieval only when instructions exist.
- Controls: §191.7 seven-arm frequency panel (full, frequency-only, random-embedding identity, frequency-bin
  substitution, top-k removal with pre-registered k grid, IDF weighting, size-matched eval); §188.8 size confound;
  RQ16-13 leakage-inflation comparison (random vs exact-group vs split-group).
- Metrics: Recall@K, MRR, nDCG@K, frequency-stratified macro Recall, reconstruction AUPRC; paired cluster bootstrap over
  split groups.
- Gates: **G35-0**, **G35-CIRC** (e.g. never headline ingredient-overlap retrieval for an IDF-Jaccard representation,
  and record that 07I family edges themselves used IDF-Jaccard ≥0.80 → circular if families are both split unit and
  target).
- Licence: explicit statistics on all rows (analysis); any learned model on `training_allowed=YES` (73,778) only.
- Output: `ledgers/representation/recipe_explicit_v1/` (partitioned sparse), `reports/step35/recipe_explicit_baselines_v1.md`.
  Compute: CPU; sparse 611k × ~5k; streamable by source partition.

### 35d Cuisine explicit rungs (C0–C2)
- Inputs: REC cuisine labels (9.81% coverage; 256 raw strings; 153/156 labelled sources single-label), cuisine ontology
  draft (Step 04 schema), source registry, 35c vectors.
- Do: C0 P(i|C); C1 specificity A_i^C with **one** pinned definition (SSOT uses C−1 at L13874 and K−1 at L14129) and
  cuisine-level IDF named distinctly from recipe-level IDF; C2 pair/triplet motifs with support thresholds; §85
  fingerprint; C3-explicit mean recipe vector.
- Tasks: cuisine→recipe retrieval; held-out prevalence reconstruction; held-out motif prediction; similarity stability
  under equal-recipe-count and size-matched resampling (§189.7–189.8). Cuisine classification only with source-holdout
  collapse test (§191.8) and disclaimer "source/book classifier" where cuisine ≈ source.
- Gate: G13-4 applies only to learned z_C (35g); for 35d, stability under matched resampling (bootstrap neighbour-overlap
  ≥ pre-registered bound†) and minimum class support†.

- Entry condition: (i) an explicit rung leaves a documented held-out failure; (ii) a non-circular supervised target

## O.1 Frozen boundary (SSOT §246, read this run, L26712–26770)
- §246.1: do not expand FlavorTwin's architecture before the shared L16 core is implemented.
- §246.2: Z* = {chemical, sensory, functional, process, culinary}; "Do not define one universal flavor-similarity scalar."
- §246.3: target → plausible ingredients → static/structural/sensory/culinary baselines → process expansion → condition
  refinement → recipe-role/context reranking → evidence/OOD/constraint gate → diverse Pareto candidates.
- §246.4: candidate = ingredient + state + process + conditions; static baselines mandatory.
- §246.5: score(i→j | recipe, role, process, quantity); compensation cannot be invented.
- §246.6: evidence classes OBSERVED_MATCH, STRUCTURAL_MATCH, SENSORY_SUPPORTED_MATCH, MODEL_ESTIMATED_MATCH,
  PROCESS_SIMULATED_MATCH, EXTRAPOLATED, UNSUPPORTED.
- §246.7: chemical similarity ≠ perceived flavour equivalence; strong sensory claims need sensory/human validation.
- §246.8: baselines random/category/ECFP/descriptors/static embeddings/static multiview/process-conditioned/
  process+recipe-context; process conditioning must beat static on held-out process-sensitive task.
- §257P FlavorTwin V2 claim checklist (L42736–42742, read this run: static baselines; calibrated transition inputs; constraints/OOD tracked; process-conditioned beats static on held-out process-sensitive task; sensory wording backed or avoided); §216.11 (L22980) defers unrestricted inverse process planning; G16-FT (L27485);
  §279.6 cultural prior P_culture only after E13E-17, may rerank, may not redefine target space (L45610–45613).
These are correct and are kept unchanged. FlavorTwin lives as a **late sub-track of Step 36** (no new step).

## O.3 Sensory and chemical limits (what FlavorTwin may and may not say)
- Molecule-level odour structure→percept prediction is credible (Lee et al. Science 381:999, 2023), but only 8 of 19
  DREAM descriptors were predicted well (Keller et al. Science 355:820, 2017); mixtures are poorly predicted from
  components (Snitz et al. PLoS CB 9:e1003184, 2013; Ravia et al. Nature 588:118, 2020, lab mixtures). **No public
  ingredient-level sensory label set** was found → SENSORY_SUPPORTED_MATCH is unreachable without a sensory study (§246.7;
  RQ16-27 "if feasible").
- Presence ≠ abundance ≠ importance: ~230 key food odorants among ~10,000 volatiles (Dunkel et al. Angew Chem 2014);
  repo has 0 odour thresholds and 0 odorant concentrations → no OAV-based "importance".
- Pairing statistics describe cultures (Ahn et al. Sci Rep 1:196, 2011; Jain, Rakhi & Bagler PLoS One 10:e0139539,
  2015 — frequency drives Indian negative pairing; Spence Food Res Int 133:109124, 2020) → "pairs well" never follows
  from shared compounds.
- Process-conditioned flavour: current EVD has nutrients/phenolics only (USDA R6, Bognár, Phenol-Explorer); no volatile
  before/after evidence → process-conditioned **flavour** claims NEED_DATA; process-conditioned **nutrient/phenolic
  state** matching is possible within validated domains only.
- Licences: FlavorGraph-derived profiles DERIVED_ONLY/NC; FooDB CC BY-NC; VCF subscription; GoodScents/Leffingwell
  unreviewed; pyrfume-data repository MIT at repo level but per-dataset terms UNVERIFIED (github.com/pyrfume/pyrfume-data,
  fetched 2026-10-22) → a public FlavorTwin benchmark (DATA-FLAVORTWIN-BENCH) may not redistribute derived profiles
  without review.

# ===== M0_data_planes =====
# M0 — Data-plane architecture review (brief §13)

Drafter: G_A · 2026-10-22 · read-only audit; nothing implemented. The 36-step plan is missing, so "owner step" is RECONSTRUCTED from SSOT, Master Plan v4.0 (MP), repo artifacts and the reader notes. Ledger counts are latest-version unique ids recounted this session with stdlib Python (`ledgers/data/*.jsonl`); line counts include version history.

## 0. Verdict

- **At the data level the planes are mostly kept apart today, but by convention and per-tool code, not by a contract.** Separation is enforced in four places: (1) the recipe-semantics parquets carry `source_plane=RECIPE`, `observation_class=TEXT_STATED` (`src/culinarystate/recipes/probe.py` L2, L197); (2) the `source_class` magnitude rule — "STRUCTURAL_RECIPE may define that a process occurred; it may NOT by itself define the measured … magnitude" (`docs/simulator_data_contract.md`; `src/culinarystate/state_graph/source_class.py`; `tests/unit/test_external_data_policy.py`); (3) `may_enter_gold_evaluation=false` for simulated rows (`registry/simulated_state_changes_schema_v1.csv`); (4) gate checks that scientific ledgers stay byte-identical when recipe-plane work runs (07H-R G4, `reports/step07/step07hr_gate_result.json`; 07I-R "scientific ledgers unchanged").
- **No JSONL ledger carries a plane field** (grep over `ledgers/schemas/*.json` for `source_plane|plane|observation_class`: 0 hits). Plane membership is implicit in the record type — and four record types are shared across planes or will be: COND, STATE/EVT, KGE and IMAP.
- **Five concrete mixing risks** need a firewall before the steps that would trigger them: (R1) recipe-stated conditions entering the evidence COND ledger via `EVT.condition_id` (Steps 16–18); (R2) one STATE ledger holding PLANNED (recipe), OBSERVED (episode) and PREDICTED (model) beliefs; (R3) KGE mixing recipe co-occurrence statistics, recipe-derived "typical temperature/duration", molecule taste imports and CoSyLab health associations in one ledger with one scalar `confidence`; (R4) IMAP `PROCESS_CHANGE` rows (419) duplicating EVD evidence (`provenance.method=DERIVED`, `evidence_ids` → EVD rows) — double counting if both are retrieved; (R5) ID-namespace collisions that blur planes: `SIM-` (similarity registry SIM-01..SIM-21 vs simulation ids in MP-1 L13), `MODEL-` (ML model card vs Step-24 formula registry), `MEAS-` (method, not measurement), `EXP-` (ML run, not scientific experiment), research `CLM` vs runtime ClaimLedger.
- **A conceptual mixing already exists in a frozen contract:** MP-1 §1.G lists `SIM-` among "Evidence" ids (`reports/h_state/state_representation_contract_v1.md` L13). SSOT §232.3 (L25264–25273) and §233.7 (L25385–25399, "Model Memory ≠ Evidence Memory") forbid this. Retro-fix 03.9.
- **Governance-level mixing:** Step 07 (an evidence-plane step) also delivered recipe-plane artifacts (07H-R recipe base, 07I-R identity) (gov §9 item 10). The data stayed separated (gate G4), so no data is contaminated; the fix is to register these artifacts in the RECIPE plane with Step 07 recorded as producer, plus a 07I-C calibration substep (r_l13e_identity), not to renumber.
- **Recommendation:** freeze `registry/data_plane_registry_v1.csv` + firewall rules FW-01…FW-16 as Step 04.6 (P0, cheap, CPU), enforce them as validators before Step 08 (evidence firewall) and before Step 16 (recipe/state firewall). No new top-level step (anti-scope-creep test B fails: home = Step 04).

## 1. Plane definitions and crosswalk

The SSOT has two partitions that disagree with the brief: §232.3 four evidence planes D^recipe, D^scientific, D^estimated, D^simulated ("can join by canonical IDs but are not interchangeable", SSOT L25264–25273); §233.7 five memory classes Source, Semantic, Episode/session, Evidence, Model (Model holds "predictions, imputations and simulations", L25387–25391). The brief §13 asks for six planes. Recommended canonical set (SSOT-compatible crosswalk; SSOT change request filed as PROPOSED_ONLY, see §7):

| Plane (code) | Holds | SSOT §233.7 class | SSOT §232.3 plane | Epistemic status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SOURCE (P-SRC) | immutable raw source records, snapshots, raw files, source manifests | Source memory | — | as-received; never edited |
| RECIPE SEMANTIC (P-REC) | normalised recipe text objects: pointers, mentions, recipe-level identity/families, planned procedure graphs (belief PLANNED) | Semantic memory | D^recipe | TEXT_STATED; never chemistry truth |
| SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE (P-EVD) | measured/compiled scientific attestations and their lineage, conditions, methods, trajectories, author-reported parameters | Evidence memory | D^scientific | tiered E1–E5 (E3 today) |
| STATE / EPISODE (P-EPI) | live session state graphs, user observations (belief OBSERVED) | Episode/session memory | — | observed in session; overrides predictions on observable fields (SSOT L25217, L25347) |
| MODEL (P-MOD) | predictions, imputations, learned embeddings, fitted project parameters, ML model cards, formula/model definitions | Model memory | D^estimated | MODEL_ESTIMATED / IMPUTED; never evidence |
| SIMULATION (P-SIM) | simulator runs, E7 synthetic priors, synthetic history | Model memory (split out) | D^simulated | SIMULATED; never evaluation truth |

Two cross-cutting **non-memory layers** that every plane joins on (not planes, but they must be named so tools do not treat them as evidence):
- REFERENCE (L-REF): controlled vocabularies and ontologies used as join keys — ING, ALIAS, PROC, TOOL, UNIT, SVAR, MOL, condition/measurement registries, mechanism registry definitions (MECH-, Step 21). A vocabulary row is a *definition*, not an observation (SSOT inv. #8/#9; §234.6 "internal IDs are authoritative; FoodOn/FDC are alignments").
- GOVERNANCE / EVALUATION (L-GOV): splits, claims, experiments, gates, datasets, human-verification queues, threshold registry. They *reference* plane records but must never feed values back into them.

# ===== M_recipe_state =====
# PART M — RECIPE-STATE ARCHITECTURE (brief §14–17, §31–32)

Drafter: G_D · 2026-10-22 · plan only. The 36-step plan document is missing; this Part is reconstructed from SSOT v15 (`SSOT Lnnnnn`), Master Plan v4.0 (`MP Lnnnn`), Detailed R&D Plan v2 (`RD Lnnnn`), repo artifacts, and the research notes `r_recipe_semantics_gold`, `r_l13e_identity`, `r_eval_splits`. Numbers marked PROPOSED_PILOT need human approval before use as gates.

## M.0 Scope, planes and permanent separations

- **Planes touched.** SOURCE MEMORY (REC, `recipe_base_v1`, immutable; D-024) → RECIPE SEMANTIC MEMORY (mentions, links, QNT, EVT/ENTITY/STATE/ALLOC/REF/GRAPH, identity) → STATE/EPISODE MEMORY (sessions, observations; C18). Recipe semantics never write into SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE MEMORY (EVD) or SIMULATION MEMORY. Every derived recipe row carries `source_plane=RECIPE`, `observation_class=TEXT_STATED`, no E-tier (D-024), and `magnitude_eligible=false` (simulator data contract `docs/simulator_data_contract.md`: STRUCTURAL_RECIPE may state that a process occurred, never its size).
- **Separations (laws).** food identity ≠ form ≠ state ≠ process ≠ quantity ≠ unit ≠ size ≠ role ≠ intermediate identity (MP L84); canonical food ≠ alias/form/state/variety/size/brand (SSOT inv. #8, L25147–25170); canonical process ≠ surface phrase/modifier (inv. #9); recipe labels ≠ chemistry truth (inv. #6); UNKNOWN ≠ 0; Silver ≠ Gold; process clock τ ≠ historical clock t (SSOT L42996–43021).
- **Three identities** (RD L327–333; MP-1 contract L6–14): concept `ING-` (reusable vocabulary) · recipe entity/lot `ENT-` (one lot, mixture, reserved portion) · entity state version `STATE-` (that entity at an event index). "Dicing does not create a new concept, but the later state must never overwrite the original mention."

## M.2 Ingredient identity vs state — hierarchy and mapping strategy (brief §14)

**Evidence.** FoodEx2 base term + facets (`A01CE#F28.A07LC`); FoodOn separates food product vs food source with facet links (LanguaL successor); Open Food Facts keeps separate taxonomies for processing, states, sizes, brands (r_recipe_semantics_gold Q4, HIGH on pattern). SSOT §234 (L25400–25499) and §257A.1 decision tree (L27873–27914) prescribe the same factorisation and a 7-way outcome (EXISTING_ALIAS · EXISTING_CONCEPT_WITH_MODIFIERS · AMBIGUOUS/POLYSEMOUS · BRAND_ALIAS/PRODUCT_VARIANT · COMPOUND_FOOD · TRUE_NEW_CONCEPT · NON_FOOD).

**Recommended hierarchy.**
1. **Identity base term** (`ING-`): food source + identity-defining part (egg yolk ≠ egg; garlic; tomato paste as DERIVED_FROM tomato; sour cream as lexicalised product). Product earns its own concept only when composition/processing/culinary meaning cannot be represented by base + declared modifiers (RD L352).
2. **Shallow is-a** ≤ 4 levels (produce › allium › onion › red onion), mandatory `parent_id` for new concepts.
3. **Orthogonal facet vocabularies** (attached to mentions/entities, not concepts): V_VARIETY · V_PART · V_FORM (whole/ground/paste/juice) · V_CUT_GEOMETRY (diced/sliced/julienne + size class) · V_STATE (raw/cooked/ripe/frozen/thawed/dried/melted) · V_MATURITY · V_PRESERVATION (canned/smoked/salted/pickled) · V_PACKING (packed/loose/drained) · V_SALT_STATE etc. (from §257A.1.1 examples, e.g. unsalted) · V_BRAND→PRODUCT layer · V_LOCALE_SENSE (corn flour UK vs US). `source_state` (as purchased: frozen) is distinct from `current_state` (thawed) and from embedded events ("thawed and squeezed dry" → events, SSOT L27916–27945).
4. **Compound foods** (`COMPOUND_FOOD` kind): optional HAS_INGREDIENT decomposition links with own evidence; never decompose a purchased compound food into assumed ingredients (RD L352).
5. **Regional/language names**: aliases with language, locale, script, transliteration, source frequency, alias_type (§238.89); era aliases for historical text (L13E RISK-E3).
6. **Unresolved**: `UNRESOLVED` / `NO_VALID_CANDIDATE` with candidate set kept (never nearest-ID fallback; RD E.2).

**Mapping strategy.** Cascade (RD L354–363, adjusted to repo evidence): exact curated alias (locale-unambiguous) → normalised alias → fuzzy char/token → frozen BGE dense top-k → (no generic cross-encoder; repo negative) → closed-set selector with NO_VALID_CANDIDATE → calibrated accept/review/unresolved routing (RD risk budget accepted-link error ≤2% PROPOSED). External crosswalks are SKOS-typed (exact/broad/narrow/related) with confidence and status: FoodOn first (open, OBO), FDC/FNDDS for nutrition/portions (by data type), FoodEx2 optional, LanguaL via FoodOn. NO_MATCH is a valid state; wrong links are worse than NO_MATCH. **Coverage is mention-weighted** with separate head/torso/tail/regional buckets (SSOT L25450–25453; target "such as 98–99%" is a declared target, not a quota).

**Rejected.** Whole-string concepts ("chopped red onion"); FoodOn-as-identity; LanguaL as primary; auto-mapping by label.

## M.3 CQPO fields and conversion policy — no fake grams (brief §15)

**Three never-collapsed problems** (SSOT §235.1 L25502–25511): deterministic physical conversion · locale-aware culinary unit interpretation · ingredient/form/packing/locale-specific volume/count→mass grounding.

**Quantity record v1** (§238.103 names + additions; RD D.1 AST): `raw_text`, `source_span`, AST node (`RATIONAL, RANGE, ADD, MULTIPLY, FRACTION_OF, REMAINDER_OF, PACKAGE_CONTENT, ALTERNATIVE, QUALITATIVE, OPEN_AMOUNT, UNKNOWN`; "500 g or 1 cup" = ALTERNATIVE, never multiplied), `value/lower/upper` as exact rationals, `quantity_kind` ≠ `dimension`, `unit_raw`, `unit_id`, `unit_system`, `unit_variant` (e.g. katori/US cup/metric cup), `locale` + `locale_evidence`, `size`, `packing`, `container` + `container_stated_mass`, qualifiers (approximate, heaped, level, packed, divided, reserved, optional, to taste, enough to cover, for dusting), **added**: `quantity_scope ∈ {INGREDIENT_LINE, INSTRUCTION_ALLOCATION, YIELD_SERVING}`, `multiplier`, `dual_expression_check` (e.g. "1 cup (240 ml)", flag on conflict), `measured_state` (raw/cooked/drained/sifted/packed — "1 cup cooked rice" ≠ raw rice), `as_purchased_vs_edible` + `edible_fraction_ref`, `reference_entity_id`/`fraction_of`/`part_of` (half the reserved sauce; juice of ½ lemon), `normalized_mass_g`, **`normalized_mass_low_g/high_g`**, `normalized_volume_ml(+low/high)`, `interval_semantics ∈ {SOURCE_RANGE, CONVERSION_UNCERTAINTY, EMPIRICAL_QUANTILES}`, `q_level` Q0–Q6, `conversion_record_id`, `conversion_path[{from,to,factor,source,evidence_id}]`, `uncertainty_source_var` (correlated splits), `unresolved_reason`, provenance.

**PortionProfile v1** (§238.129 + repo POR): ingredient_id, **state, form, size_class**, packing, portion_value/unit, unit_locale, mass_g, **mass_low_g, mass_high_g**, conversion_class (= Q-level), source_type, source_record, **sample_count, source_diversity**, licence, verification (human, D-006). Rule: never merge portion values across states/forms/locales until compatibility is established (§257F.2 L34713).

**Grounding ladder** (SSOT §235.3 L25520–25531, reconciled with §257A.2 L27993–27999): Q0 exact physical (deterministic; temperature affine — RD D.2) → Q1 authoritative portion (FNDDS FoodWeights/FDC by data type) → Q2 authoritative density (FAO/INFOODS Density v2) → Q3 multi-source verified estimate (incl. "other approved national table", which §257A.2 adds without a Q-level → map to Q3 with `national_table` flag; SSOT change request) → Q4 recipe-corpus empirical distribution (flagged, never in totals without flag; repo POR.basis `CONVENTION` maps here or to Q3 — needs ruling) → Q5 model estimate **only if the task explicitly permits** → Q6 UNKNOWN. Implementation: a decision layer **selects** a POR record (or NO_COMPATIBLE_RECORD); deterministic code computes (RD E14.14 pattern).

**Policy.** Gold annotators never convert units; Gold for grounding = which POR record applies, or UNKNOWN (SSOT §237.1). Ranges stay ranges (no midpoint, ever). Qualitative quantities stay qualitative (pinch/handful/to taste; SSOT L25538). No authoritative source was found for Indian household measures (katori, glass) or verbal quantities (r_recipe_semantics_gold Q6) → interval with locale evidence or UNKNOWN. Historical units (gill, teacupful) carry `unit_system_era` + conversion uncertainty; never force modern FDC portions (L13E RISK-E4). Quantity encoder downstream uses masks, never zeros (§235.7 L25561–25570). **Invariant: grams invented without an evidence route = 0** (RD L592–599; MP SX-10-02).

**Gates.** G16-QTY (L27452) operationalised: deterministic unit fixtures 100% (property tests exist, `tests/property/test_quantity_properties.py`); invented-value audit 0/≥300 stratified outputs; per-Q-level coverage reported (not gated); interval calibration reported only where distributional with authoritative ground truth.

## M.4 Process / tool hierarchy depth (brief §16)

**Evidence.** No widely adopted ontology of cooking actions or kitchen tools; FoodOn processes and LanguaL G/H / FoodEx2 F28 describe the food, not procedural actions (r_recipe_semantics_gold Q5, MEDIUM). SSOT: compact processes + modifiers; do not force 10,000 processes (L25461); leaf-vs-modifier decided by experiment (L28068–28074).

**Process (3 levels + orthogonal axes).**
1. **Family** ~15–20 (heat/transfer-mode families; current 18 minus housekeeping) — mandatory `parent_id` from leaf.
2. **Canonical process** ~150–300 (repo 147 ACTION today; target ≥300 per `max_plan_consensus.md` L21) — definition, required condition axes (106 already have them), typical medium/tool, safety-critical fields (MP W11 template).
3. **Surface aliases** unbounded, language-tagged, raw verb always kept; explicit UNMAPPED allowed.
- **Modifiers** (SSOT §257A.3): intensity (gentle/vigorous), granularity (finely/roughly), geometry (cube/julienne + size class), medium (water/oil/steam/air/dry pan), endpoint reference, duration class.
- **Transformation mode** (separate axis): MECHANICAL · THERMAL · CHEMICAL_CURING · BIOCHEMICAL_FERMENTATION · TRANSFER · TEMPORAL_REST. Manual vs thermal vs biochemical is this axis, not the family.
- **Endpoints** move out of PROC (9 ENDPOINT rows) into `V_ENDPOINT` (stop criteria/observations: golden, tender, soft-ball stage). "Bake until golden" = BAKE + endpoint_ref=golden, time/temperature UNKNOWN (§257H.5).
- **Mechanism families** on PROC stay AI_DRAFTED candidate-effect links for Step 22, never evidence (SSOT L26136).

**Tool (category → tool → alias).** Categories: heat source · cookware · vessel/container · utensil · appliance · measure. Attribute axes: material/coating, heat-transfer mode, pressure capability, capacity, geometry. Safety limits UNKNOWN unless manufacturer/authority evidence (MP X1 L1945). Events carry `tool_roles` (INSTRUMENT / CONTAINER / HEAT_SOURCE / MEASURE). External links (Wikidata QIDs exist in `registry/tools/tool_wikidata_v1.csv`) are crosswalks only.

**Rejected.** Deep (>4-level) process taxonomy; flat 10k process list; mapping modifiers to separate leaves by default.

## M.5 Recipe identity, incorporating 07I-R (brief §17)

**Completed (07I-R, S134, D-025).** Level A DUPLICATE_GROUP deterministic (raw hash, content sha, normalised text hash, canonical URL): 1,039 exact groups. Level B RECIPE_FAMILY PROVISIONAL_STAR_V1 (IDF-ingredient Jaccard ≥0.80 ∧ title Jaccard ≥0.50 ∧ (shingle ≥0.30 ∨ process-seq ≥0.70 with ≥3 processes) ∧ no explicit cuisine conflict; star, no chaining; calibrated=false). Level C DISH_FAMILY_CANDIDATE (46,697). Relation classes: only EXACT_BINARY_COPY / EXACT_NORMALIZED_COPY / MIRRORED_COPY coalesce. Gold firewall: 50 Gold-indexed, 0 same-group non-Gold, 2 with family relatives.

**Relation ladder (target vocabulary).** EXACT copy → NEAR_DUPLICATE_SAME_RECIPE → SCALED_VARIANT → MINOR_FORMULATION_VARIANT (family) → SAME_DISH_DIFFERENT_RECIPE (dish family) → REGIONAL_VARIANT / SAME_DISH_DIFFERENT_AUTHOR_OR_ERA (historical; SSOT §264.7 L43476–43483; L13E only) → RELATED_DISH → DISTINCT; plus COPY_MUTATE_PARENT (L13E, documented lineage only). Typed relations are stored as edges and **never coalesced** except exact copies; source recipes stay immutable (law).

**Two derived products (opposite cost asymmetries; r_l13e_identity Q8, r_eval_splits Q4).**
- `recipe_identity_relations_v1` — **precision-oriented**, non-transitive (Broder 1997: resemblance is not transitive), used for consensus/family views and cultural analysis; false merges erase variants.
- `recipe_split_groups_v1` — **recall-oriented** leakage components: connected components over exact groups ∪ calibrated near-dup edges at OP-SPLIT ∪ dish-family candidates ∪ cross-source copies; giant-component guard (Lee et al. ACL 2022 saw a 250,933-document cluster) with fallback to sub-blocking by dish key and reporting of residual cross-split similarity (max IDF-Jaccard test→train). Explicit-cuisine-disagreement pairs are never auto-merged as identity but **may** share a split group.

**Calibration of the 400-pair packet (07I-C; human-gated; parallel to 08–15; must pass before any recipe-level test split is frozen).** Literature thresholds (0.8 Jaccard/edit; SourcererCC 0.8/0.7; RecipeNLG F1-optimal cosine vs same-URL proxy) are tool defaults/proxies, not recipe-identity thresholds (r_l13e_identity Q6, HIGH); SSOT §264.1/264.8 forbids fixed rules.
1. Pre-register label mapping before unsealing: Y_copy = {SAME_RECIPE_COPY, SAME_RECIPE_MINOR_VARIANT}; Y_dish = Y_copy ∪ {SAME_DISH_DIFFERENT_RECIPE}; RELATED/DISTINCT negative; UNCERTAIN excluded with ± sensitivity.
2. Independent blind labels (Kush, Parv), files hash-locked before adjudication; κ and Gwet AC1 on 6-class, Y_copy, Y_dish; per-stratum descriptive.
3. v1 = development/calibration set only: Horvitz–Thompson weights from `stratum_pool_size`; low-capacity monotone calibrator (≤8-feature logistic; no isotonic at n≈400); grouped CV by dish family ∪ source.
4. Declare OP-MERGE (high precision; PROPOSED Wilson LB ≥ 0.90) and OP-SPLIT (high recall; PROPOSED ≥ 0.95 within kept pairs).
5. Build **sealed v2** (~300–400 pairs, new seed): ≥100 predicted positives per operating point; recall probes for pairs completeness (Christen 2012) — skipped over-cap LSH buckets (4,745), sub-4-ingredient recipes (Amendment A1), scored-but-not-kept pairs, random base-rate pairs; ≥30 scaled variants (S08 missing in v1 — investigate cause first); ≥60 cultural/regional pairs with a cuisine-knowledgeable reviewer where possible; full text or explicit truncation marks.
6. Freeze `recipe_identity_calibration_v1.json` and `recipe_split_groups_v1.parquet`; run RQ16-13 (random vs group split inflation) on the first downstream model.
- Precision CI reality: 40 pairs per stratum at p=0.95 → Wilson 0.835–0.986 (r_l13e_identity Q7); v1 cannot be a per-stratum sealed test.
- **Fail path:** never block splits — use the conservative permissive grouping (exact ∪ provisional family ∪ dish-family candidate ∪ same-normalised-title components, or source-level) and keep descriptive distances only (G13E-07 fail action).
- **Gold leakage firewall:** a Gold recipe's SPLIT_GROUP is excluded from every training set, Silver sample, Gold-Light queue, prompt demo and retrieval exemplar; 7/40 old Gold have exact-title twins in the bulk corpus → title-twin flag on the Gold index.
- **Cross-source historical copies:** 3,431 FOODCOM+GUTENBERG same-title groups with 0 exact cross-source groups → web re-posts of historical recipes are a leakage channel for any temporal claim (L13E G13E-02).

## M.6 Instruction semantic schema — EVT / ENTITY / STATE event sourcing

**Representation.** Typed entities + DAG with intermediates and a final-dish root + implicit-argument links + per-step state-change tuples (Mori 2014; Yamakata 2020; RISeC; SSOT §233 is a superset). Event-sourced: current state derived from ordered events; no destructive overwrite; replay, correction, causal inspection, merge/split accounting (SSOT L25351–25358).

**INST** (per instruction step, stored separately from events; MP X2 L1951–1966): raw span, section id, sentence spans, language/script, normalised verb candidates, quantity/time/temperature mentions, endpoint phrase, implicit subject/object, coreference pointers, negation/optionality, sequence relation.

**EVT v1:** event_id, recipe_id, inst_id, step_index, ordinal, `text_order` + `depends_on[]` (execution DAG separate from text order), `event_kind ∈ {ACTION, ENDPOINT_CHECK, OBSERVATION, CONDITIONAL, WAIT_REST, CONTROL}`, process_id + process_family_id + action_raw (kept when UNMAPPED), process_modifiers{intensity, granularity, geometry, medium, endpoint_ref}, transformation_mode, input/output entity-version ids, `tool_roles[]`, medium, `implicit_args[{role, resolution_ref, provenance}]`, `alternative_group_id`, `modality ∈ {REQUIRED, OPTIONAL, NEGATED, CONDITIONAL, HYPOTHETICAL}` + raw cue, `temporal_relation ∈ {SEQUENTIAL, PARALLEL, OVERLAPS, UNTIL, REPEAT_UNTIL}` (control constructs — "repeat until smooth" never invents an iteration count), `condition_profile_id` → COND (07H; per-axis MEASURED/RANGE/UNKNOWN/NOT_APPLICABLE; setpoint ≠ product temperature; "boiling" never 100 °C; months never seconds), duration/temperature raw + normalised with `clock=TAU_PROCESS`, `endpoint_state_refs` (stop criteria), `endpoint_leakage_flag`, `trajectory ∈ {PLANNED, OBSERVED_SESSION, PREDICTED}`, `omitted_step_candidate{rule_id, precedent_ids}` (outside the observed graph), `allocation_ids[]`, span, provenance triple, validation_flags. Descriptors needed by Steps 26–27 captured as TEXT_STATED when present: water:food ratio, lid/cover, start mode (cold vs boiling water), piece size.

**ENTITY v1:** entity_id, recipe_id, `entity_type ∈ {INGREDIENT_LOT, INTERMEDIATE, MIXTURE, RESERVED_PORTION, DISCARDED_PORTION, TOOL_CONTENTS}`, canonical_food_id (nullable), label, ordinal, `parent_entity_ids[]`, `created_by_event_id`, `consumed_by_event_id`, `lifecycle ∈ {ACTIVE, RESERVED, INCORPORATED, DISCARDED, SERVED, UNRESOLVED}` ("incorporation ≠ the material vanished", RD L584), facets.

**STATE v1** (belief per field, SSOT §233.2 L25338–25345): state_id, entity_id, state_version, previous_state_id, produced_by_event_id, overrides_state_id, event_index, `belief`, and per-field `{value | interval | category | UNKNOWN, unit, origin_provenance (8-class §239.1), field_status (KNOWN/UNKNOWN/NOT_APPLICABLE/CONFLICTING/CENSORED), claim_route (EXPLICIT/INFERRED_RULE/INFERRED_LLM/MODEL/SIMULATED), evidence_or_model_ref, uncertainty, observable_in_session, observation_source}`. Three layers: (i) existence/creation/consumption, (ii) location/container, (iii) attributes from SVAR (closed vocabulary + OTHER). Qualitative thermal/texture/visual states only; numeric only when supported (RD L383–401). UNKNOWN-capable history fields for Step 23 (enzyme_activity_state, cell_integrity, time_since_disruption, thermal_dose, oxygen_exposure) — **never filled from recipe text** ("No pH/water-activity value appears unless explicit/external/model/simulated provenance is declared", L26289).

**ALLOC / REF / GRAPH.** ALLOC: parent/child entity, fraction (exact rational or interval), `basis ∈ {MASS, VOLUME, COUNT, PORTION_FRACTION_ONLY}`, kind (SPLIT/RESERVE/DISCARD/RECOMBINE), event_id, correlated uncertainty var. REF: mention span, kind (PRONOUN/ZERO_ANAPHORA/DEFINITE_NP/REMAINDER/PART_OF), resolves_to (entity ids or unresolved candidate set — never forced, C2 rule). GRAPH: edges per SSOT relation enum (MERGES_INTO, SPLITS_INTO, RESERVED_AS, DISCARDED_FROM, RECOMBINED_WITH, TRANSFORMS_INTO, TRANSFERRED_TO, PART_OF, LOCATED_IN, OBSERVED_AS; L25369–25378), replay_sha256, session_id.

**Engine invariants** (RD L592–599; SSOT §240.2): spans round-trip; every ingredient-list lot accounted; nothing used before produced or after discard; split fractions ≤ 1 per basis; mass balance only when all terms known else `unknown`; inferred events never feed explicit-only queries; invented grams = 0; issue codes instead of silent clamping (RD D.9). Deterministic replay: identical inputs ⇒ identical snapshot hash.

**Exports.** `transition_tuples_v1` (for 22/29; occurrence only, `magnitude_eligible=false`, UNKNOWN masks, endpoint-leakage flag, split_group_id) and `prefix_packets_v1` (for 36; online prefix, no future leakage).

**Evaluation of state** (ProPara/OpenPI2.0 lesson): exact match per canonical attribute with UNKNOWN as a class, salience-weighted and unweighted, three layers scored separately; engine fidelity (oracle events) separated from predicted-event accuracy.

## M.7 Corpus tiering of the 612k base and sampling strategy (brief §31)

Unit of independence = SPLIT_GROUP (recall-oriented; M.5). Assign groups to tiers and splits **before** any sampling (SSOT L28336; P-A12).

| Tier | Size | Processing | Selection | Use | Never |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T0 weak corpus | all 611,714 exact reps | deterministic only (07H-R parsers, lexicons, frozen NER/linker, rule events); streamed, partitioned, checkpointed, resumable | all | vocab/alias statistics, long-tail discovery, parser pretraining (licence permitting), Step-35 explicit baselines, L13E 35-E | as Gold; as evaluation |
| T1 Silver | 10k pilot (1k→5k→10k) → 25k → 60k only if utility curve rises; 100k never by default | selected Step-17 cascade (local LLM + validators V1–V6, two-model disagreement, confident-learning flags) | stratified probability sample over §236.3 strata (+ licence), **one rep per SPLIT_GROUP**, disproportionate allocation with recorded inclusion probabilities; Food.com share capped (PROPOSED ≤50%; it is 85% of the base); Deep-Gold groups excluded | parser training/distillation, statistics, state graphs | dev/test/calibration |
| T2 Gold-Light | 3–5k **units** (lines/mentions/events), not recipes | single human verification, model-assisted allowed and logged (MODEL_ASSISTED_HUMAN_REVIEWED); ≥15–20% double for IAA | ≤70% uncertainty/disagreement/frequency-impact queue + ≥30% random | linker/quantity/process tuning, validator calibration, AL, B2 training | final test; scoring the model that suggested its labels |
| T3 Deep Gold | staged DG-0 30 (design) → DG-1 100–200 → DG-2 ~500 (before Step-36 calibration) → 750–1,000 only if CI analysis requires | 2 independent blank annotations + adjudication + validators; model output hidden | frozen probability sample from SPLIT_GROUPs held out of T1/T2; hard strata (§237.5) oversampled with weights | dev / calibration / sealed test; RAG state cases | AL selection; model pre-fill |
| Synthetic/Bronze | as needed | generated | — | stress tests only | any real evaluation (inv. #15) |

**Sampling details.** Strata (SSOT §236.3 L25603–25618): source domain; cuisine/region where labels exist (only 9.81% labelled; Food.com 0%; Gutenberg labels are book-level → stratify by `cuisine_label_level`); dish category (Food.com RecipeCategory/Keywords — not yet ingested); process family; ingredient-count bin; step-count/graph-complexity bin; quantity completeness; rare/regional ingredient bin; language/locale (100% English — report as limitation); licence/release constraints; failure/troubleshooting presence. Report Horvitz–Thompson-weighted population metrics **and** per-stratum metrics with SPLIT_GROUP cluster-bootstrap CIs. Batch checkpoints every 5k–10k (§236.6, 11 audits incl. near-duplicate regrouping). Per-batch human audit n≈300 stratified → zero failures bound fabricated-value rate < 1% at 95% (rule of three); ±2% error estimates need ≈460.

**Licence overlay.** training_allowed = YES only for Gutenberg (73,955); Food.com/TASTEset/A1 UNKNOWN (535,151) pending H2; Wikibooks CC BY-SA (share-alike). Until H2: T1 for training restricted to licence-cleared sources (bias reported); analysis-only Silver on Food.com requires explicit confirmation of S116 "LOCAL research use only". No recipe text to external services.

**Scale gate.** §257P P-A1…P-A15 (L42705–42723): run the 10k pilot with all items except P-A11 (cost/reannotation — a pilot output); all 15 before >10k (reconciles SSOT "before 60k–100k" with MP B07 "before past 10k", MP L386). Growth only if Silver improves DG-dev by a pre-registered margin (RQ16-09; SSOT stop rule L27490–27501).

## M.8 Gold design (brief §32)

**Requirements from evidence.** Anchoring is real and inflates LLM scores (Schroeder et al. 2025; Choi et al. 2024 43.9% → 71.5%); repo already has AI-anchored Gold (D-016/D-017) and two provenance-invalid human gates (07H v1–v3; linker byte-identical files) → independence must be **technically enforced**.

**Protocol (SSOT §237.2 L25690–25702 + enforcement, r_eval_splits R-6).**
1. Source freeze + checksum; packets issued per annotator with separate IDs; no model/Silver output shown (Deep Gold).
2. Per-item start/end timestamps; labels hash-committed before the other file is opened.
3. Automatic provenance-validity check (file mtimes, identical-distribution test, authorship) before any human gate counts — `counts_as_human_gate` in the gate JSON (07H pattern).
4. Automatic disagreement report → adjudication (third reviewer/expert for cultural/regional and failure cases) with who/why/version; pre- and post-adjudication labels kept.
5. Deterministic validators + engine replay → lock → partition by SPLIT_GROUP (dev / calibration / sealed test; four partitions incl. calibration, §257A.15 L28336) → sealed test hash + access log; never move items after any test result (L28338).

**Agreement (SSOT §237.3 per task; never one pooled score).** Krippendorff α (or span/edge F1) ≥ 0.80 for fields used in final claims; 0.667–0.80 → handbook revision and re-calibration on new items; < 0.667 → redesign or drop the field from Gold claims (PROPOSED_PILOT; Krippendorff 2004 convention). Always report raw agreement, prevalence and per-class/specific agreement (kappa paradox, Feinstein & Cicchetti 1990), recipe-cluster bootstrap CIs, n_clusters. RD targets used as PROPOSED_PILOT: core spans ≥0.90, ACTION/TOOL/DURATION ≥0.85, ENDPOINT/FORM/INTERMEDIATE ≥0.80, edges/coref ≥0.75, implicit args ≥0.65 (RD L518–529). Identity labels: κ on Y_copy ≥ 0.70 + Gwet AC1 (PROPOSED).

**Sizes (CI-driven; own arithmetic in research notes).**
| Task | Unit | DG/GL size | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Events/edges/coref/merge-split | recipe | DG-1 200 (fallback 100) | ≈2,000 events, effective n 540–1,050 → ±0.03 event F1 |
| State trajectories | recipe | 60 of DG-1 at depth A4 | pilot scale; widen in DG-2 |
| Ingredient-line structure | line | ~1,500 lines (DG-1 lines + catalog) | exact-match ±2% |
| Quantity parse | line | §257D catalog (answer keys to author) + 1,000 stratified real lines | rare types oversampled |
| Portion-record selection | line | 300–500 Gold-Light | ±4% |
| Entity linking | mention | 2,000–3,000 Gold-Light by frequency bucket | ±4–5% per bucket |
| Process/tool mapping | mention | 1,000 process + 500 tool | B05 ≥95% gate ±1.4% |
| Duplicate identity | pair | 400 v1 (dev) + 300–400 v2 (sealed) | see M.5 |
| Condition audit (07H) | condition | packet v4, 100 rows ×2, rare codes oversampled | specific agreement |
| RAG/system claims (Step 36) | item | ≥240 locked for a 10-pp paired claim | ≈155 needed at 20% discordance |
| Calibration (Step 36) | item | several hundred per rung for α=5% guarantees | Clopper–Pearson; zero errors <1% needs 299 |

**Active learning.** Only for Gold-Light queues, with ≥30% random items (Lowell et al. 2019); Deep Gold is a frozen probability sample; AL picks never enter sealed sets. Confident learning (cleanlab) flags Silver label errors.

**Anti-anchoring rules.** Deep Gold blank; model output revealed only after the independent pass and logged; `annotation_mode`, `seen_model_output` on every record; model-assisted labels never score the model family that suggested them (pilot_20 was drafted by GPT-5.6 Sol — D-016); LLM-as-annotator allowed only for Silver/Gold-Light after an alt-test-style validation per task (Calderon, Reichart & Dror ACL 2025).

**Re-tiering now.** The 40 existing Gold recipes → `MODEL_ASSISTED_HUMAN_REVIEWED` (Gold-Light); remove calibration eligibility from GOLD_PENDING in tier registry v2 (aligns with inv. #14 and §242.3).

**Human-time budget (UNVERIFIED; DG-0 measures).** 30–90 min per recipe per annotator at Deep depth; DG-1 200 at A2 (+60 at A4) ≈ 300–750 person-hours incl. adjudication; fallback 100 recipes ≈ half. This is the dominant bottleneck of Phase D and competes with Step 09–11 evidence verification for the same two people.

## M.9 Backward / forward requirement propagation (brief §38–39)

- **Pushed back:** 03 (three identities, 3-axis field metadata, τ/t clock tag, UNKNOWN-capable history fields); 04 (annotation-mode provenance classes, never-score-on-suggested-labels rule, SPLIT enum extension, calibration needs independent Gold); 06 (SRC + licence for Food.com, TASTEset, FNDDS, INFOODS, USDA yields; training/external-service/release flags; H2); 07 (condition audit v4 blind; months→seconds confirmation); 07H-R (derived table: AuthorId, DatePublished, Keywords, RecipeCategory, servings/yield, cuisine label level; Gutenberg Issued = digitisation date); 07I-R (07I-C calibration + split groups).
- **Promised forward:** 22 (event kind, process + modifiers, medium, tool roles, condition profile, endpoint, entity facets); 23 (UNKNOWN-capable history state); 26–27 (TEXT_STATED descriptors: duration, water ratio, lid, start mode, piece size); 29 (transition tuples, occurrence-only); 34b (qualitative Gold trajectories, optional); 35 (masked quantities, role + provenance, typed state, event table, per-field extraction error, split groups, servings); 36 (prefix packets, history, sessions, DG-2 calibration cases); L13E 35-E (historical block, lineage/variant IDs).

## M.10 Failure paths (brief §40)

| Failure | Consequence | Response |
|---|---|---|
| DG-0 α < 0.667 on core fields twice | schema incoherent | stop; redesign; fields demoted to Gold-Light |
| Step 17 no rung beats B0/B1 | learned extraction not justified | ship deterministic cascade + review queue; Silver limited to ingredient/quantity layers |
| Invented grams/T/t > 0 | fabrication | block that route until validator fixed |
| Engine fidelity < 0.95 with oracle events | engine wrong | fix before any export |
| Deep Gold provenance invalid | gate NOT_COUNTED | re-issue packets; no claims |
| Human capacity < 100 DG recipes | CIs too wide | NEED_HUMAN_CAPACITY; claims descriptive; G16-CAL deferred |
| 07I-C fails | split groups uncalibrated | conservative permissive grouping (never blocks splits); descriptive identity distances |
| Silver utility < δ | no scaling benefit | stop at current size; retain negative result |
| H2 negative for training | licence | analysis-only Silver; training on Gutenberg/Wikibooks only (bias reported) |

## M.11 Residual uncertainties (cannot be resolved by more reading)

Minutes per Deep-Gold recipe; achievable α on implicit arguments/state attributes; local-LLM extraction quality and throughput; CPU throughput of frozen DeBERTa over ~5M ingredient lines; Silver utility curve; pairs-completeness of the capped identity candidate generator; H2 outcomes; POR coverage for regional/historical units (expect Q6-heavy). All are settled by DG-0, the 07I-C labels, a CPU timing pilot and the 1k/5k/10k pilot — empirical work is cheaper than further literature (brief §8 rule 5).
